items.title: Empyema Due to Listeria monocytogenes in a Patient With Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is an uncommon cause of pleural empyema, particularly in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Disease and treatment-related immunosuppression increases susceptibility to invasive listeriosis, which carries significant mortality. A 78-year-old man with seropositive RA treated with methotrexate and low-dose corticosteroids presented with fever, hypotension, pleuritic chest pain, and weakness. Laboratory tests showed leukocytosis, neutrophilia, and elevated C-reactive protein. Imaging revealed a left pleural effusion with lower-lobe collapse. Thoracentesis drained 800 mL of exudative fluid, and cultures of pleural fluid and blood isolated L. monocytogenes . Cranial CT and lumbar puncture performed due to neurological symptoms were normal. High-dose ampicillin plus cotrimoxazole was administered for 7 days, followed by ampicillin monotherapy to complete a total of 14 days of antibiotic treatment, achieving progressive clinical and radiological improvement. Empyema caused by L. monocytogenes is rare and occurs mainly in immunocompromised hosts, with only isolated cases described in RA. This case underscores the need to consider Listeria infection in immunosuppressed RA patients presenting with pleural empyema. La inmunosupresión relacionada con la enfermedad y su tratamiento aumenta la susceptibilidad a listeriosis invasiva, con significativa mortalidad. Un varón de 78 años con AR seropositiva tratado con metotrexato y corticoides a bajas dosis presentó fiebre, hipotensión, dolor torácico pleurítico y debilidad. items.title: A dual-track strategy: multi-target, bidirectional modulation of uric acid biosynthesis and renal elimination by natural products-molecular insights.
items.abstract: Hyperuricemia (HUA) arises primarily from increased urate production and an imbalance in extra-renal and renal urate excretion, and is accompanied by oxidative stress, inflammatory activation, and tissue injury. Such a networked pathophysiology constrains the utility of single-target intervention strategies. While currently used single-target urate-lowering agents can effectively reduce serum urate, limitations remain in indication selection, combination therapy, safety, and long-term adherence. Natural bioactive small molecules, characterized by multi-target actions and bidirectional regulation, have emerged as a valuable avenue for the integrated prevention and management of HUA and gout. This review summarizes urate-lowering natural products across multiple structural classes-including triterpenoids, flavonoids, phenolic acids, alkaloids, polyphenols, and anthraquinones-outlining their principal pharmacological mechanisms. In line with an 'efficacy-developability co-optimization' concept, we further discuss strategies for subsequent lead optimization of natural-product-derived scaffolds, aiming to support the discovery of novel urate-lowering leads and the development of multi-target anti-gout agents.

items.title: Anakinra for the Treatment of Severe Still's Disease Complicated With Macrophage Activation Syndrome.
items.abstract: To investigate the efficacy and safety of add-on anakinra for severe Still's disease complicated by macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) in a real-world setting. Outcomes were CID, remission, and four EULAR/PReS-aligned targets, assessed at baseline, Day 7, Week 4, Month 3, and Month 6. Glucocorticoid (GC) dose was standardized to prednisone-equivalent mg/kg/day. Eight women (mean age 29.9 ± 12.8 years) were included, and anakinra was initiated at the time of MAS diagnosis in six patients, 2 months after MAS diagnosis in one and 2 months before MAS onset in one. Of the seven patients starting anakinra at or after MAS onset, all achieved Targets 1 and 2 and CID at a median of 1.5 months (range 1-5), and all maintained remission for ≥ 6 months; no severe adverse events were observed. Mean prednisone-equivalent dose fell from 1.63 ± 0.59 to 0.16 ± 0.09 mg/kg/day (p < 0.01). Four patients discontinued anakinra within 6 months for reasons of cost and access rather than disease flare. Add-on therapy with anakinra was associated with rapid achievement of EULAR/PReS targets, sustained remission, and substantial GC sparing in severe Still's disease-associated MAS.

items.title: Hydroxychloroquine therapy and its impact on bone mineral density among systemic lupus erythematosus patients: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) are at increased risk of osteoporosis due to chronic inflammation, prolonged glucocorticoid (GC) exposure, and treatment-related factors. Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ), a cornerstone of SLE therapy, has shown conflicting effects on bone health. This study examined the association between HCQ use and bone mineral density (BMD) in SLE. A cross-sectional study of 213 SLE patients was conducted at Dr. Soetomo General Academic Hospital. BMD was assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and classified using WHO criteria. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and treatment-related variables were collected. Group comparisons employed chi-square and non-parametric tests, while ordinal logistic regression identified independent predictors of reduced BMD. Among 213 patients, 22.5% had normal BMD, 51.2% osteopenia, and 26.3% osteoporosis. Independent predictors of reduced BMD were older age (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.01-1.09), higher cumulative GC exposure (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.02-1.12), and lower BMI (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.80-0.98). Importantly, the use of HCQ has been linked to a protective effect against osteoporosis (OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.22-0.97, P = 0.040). Neither SLEDAI scores nor complement/ESR levels were significantly associated with BMD. Low BMD is highly prevalent in SLE and is strongly influenced by age, GC exposure, and BMI. HCQ use was linked to a protective effect on bone health, plausibly mediated by anti-resorptive, antioxidant, and glucocorticoid-sparing properties. Although a causal relationship between these two variables cannot yet be established, this association underscores the need for further well-designed longitudinal or interventional studies.

items.title: Development and Preliminary Psychometric Validation of the Gout Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (G-KAP) Questionnaire: An Asia-Pacific Multicenter Study.
items.abstract: To develop and undertake preliminary psychometric validation of the Gout Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (G-KAP) Questionnaire for patients with gout in multiple Asia-Pacific clinical settings. Six development experts and nine relevance experts reviewed the English 56-question instrument. Analyses included 312 baseline participants from 10 countries and 117 paired assessments; 149 participants formed an additional recruitment-wave subset. Language assistance involved oral explanation without a fixed translation script. We evaluated content relevance, keyed knowledge reliability, item-level stability, and exploratory structure using explicit coding and missing-data rules. S-CVI/Ave was 0.998 across 68 rated rows. The 19-indicator knowledge score averaged 56.1% ± 20.3%; KR-20 was 0.770 and common-factor omega 0.764. Absolute-agreement single-measure ICC was 0.763 (95% bootstrap CI 0.635-0.857); mean retest increase was 2.34 percentage points (p = 0.037). Numeric attitude ICCs ranged 0.345-0.838. Among 303 complete cases for 38 exploratory indicators, full-matrix and common-factor parallel analyses suggested 7 and 11 dimensions. The seven-factor comparison model included two weak two-item factors and ambiguous cross-loadings. The English G-KAP shows strong expert-rated relevance and encouraging preliminary knowledge-score reliability. Oral-assistance variability, unequal recruitment and uncertain dimensionality limit interpretation. Cross-cultural validity, measurement invariance, attitude/practice composite scores and clinical effectiveness are unestablished. Standardized administration, linguistic adaptation and independent confirmatory evaluation are needed before cross-country comparison or subscale development.

items.title: Screening of Active Ingredients From Ficus tikoua Bur. Against Rheumatoid Arthritis and Their Enrichment Using a β-Cyclodextrin-Based Monolith.
items.abstract: Ficus tikoua Bur., a perennial creeping woody liana belonging to the genus Ficus (Moraceae), has been traditionally used in combination therapies for rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This study aimed to screen active components from F. tikoua Bur. against RA. Prior to activity testing, compounds with appropriate polarity and size were enriched by a homemade β-cyclodextrin-based monolithic material when adjusting the polarity of the enrichment mobile phase. Anti-inflammatory activity evaluations of different fractions were conducted using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Results showed that the compounds in F. tikoua Bur. had no significant effect on RAW264.7 cell viability while effectively reducing secretion levels of inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and TNF-α. When a mixture of methanol and water (30:70, v/v) was used as the enrichment mobile phase, those components adsorbed on the monolith exhibited optimal inhibition effects on IL-6 and TNF-α production. Further separation and LC-MS analysis of the most active fraction, combined with literature data, 4-hydroxy-3,5-bis(3'-methyl-2-butenyl) benzoic acid-O-β-D-glucopyranoside may be the primary anti-inflammatory constituent. Optimization of enrichment conditions revealed that the monolithic material achieved an enrichment factor of 15.352 for the screened compound.

items.title: Autoimmune Conversion of Hashimoto's Thyroiditis to Graves' Disease With Immune Pancytopenia in a Patient With Seropositive Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Diagnostic and Therapeutic Conundrum.
items.abstract: Autoimmune conversion of Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) to Graves' disease (GD) is an uncommon phenomenon. The coexistence of GD, seropositive rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and pancytopenia presents a rare diagnostic and therapeutic challenge, particularly when antithyroid drug (ATD) therapy is contemplated in the presence of pre-existing cytopenias. A 66-year-old woman with a four-year history of hypothyroidism on levothyroxine replacement and long-standing seropositive RA presented with generalized weakness, altered bowel habits, and insomnia. Serial thyroid function tests (TFTs) had demonstrated progressive suppression of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), necessitating dose reduction and eventual discontinuation of levothyroxine. Evaluation revealed thyrotoxicosis with elevated free thyroxine (FT4), free triiodothyronine (FT3), raised antithyroid peroxidase and TSH receptor antibodies, diffuse goiter with increased vascularity on Doppler ultrasonography, and diffusely increased uptake on thyroid scintigraphy, confirming Graves' disease. Concurrent investigations demonstrated pancytopenia with elevated liver enzymes and mild splenomegaly. Given the presence of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis and the exclusion of alternative causes of pancytopenia, an immune-mediated mechanism leading to bone marrow suppression was suspected. After treatment with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, carbimazole was cautiously initiated with close hematological monitoring. The patient showed progressive clinical and hematological improvement. This case highlights the rare transition from Hashimoto's thyroiditis to Graves' disease in a patient with seropositive RA and immune-mediated pancytopenia. It underscores the importance of considering autoimmune thyroid conversion in previously hypothyroid patients with persistent TSH suppression and demonstrates that carefully monitored antithyroid therapy can be safely administered despite pre-existing pancytopenia within a multidisciplinary care framework.

items.title: Early Manifestations of Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), a rare autoimmune disease formerly known as Wegener's granulomatosis, is characterized by systemic necrotizing vasculitis that primarily affects small- to medium-sized vessels. Classically, GPA manifests in the respiratory tract and kidneys; however, its early symptoms can be nonspecific, complicating timely diagnosis. This report describes the case of a 43-year-old Caucasian male presenting with progressive polyarthralgia, intermittent fever, weight loss, and other systemic symptoms over three months. Initial clinical findings, including night sweats, fatigue, and a dry cough, were nonspecific and prompted further diagnostic investigations. His condition progressed with worsening anemia, declining kidney function, and elevated inflammatory markers. Diagnostic evaluation, including serologic testing and renal biopsy, ultimately confirmed the diagnosis of GPA with pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis. This report underscores the importance of comprehensive history-taking, thorough physical examination, and a systemic approach to clinical evaluation. It highlights the critical role of primary care physicians in recognizing subtle, systemic symptoms that may point to an underlying autoimmune disease and coordinating early referrals for appropriate diagnostic testing. Timely recognition of GPA can improve outcomes, particularly when appropriate treatment is initiated promptly.

items.title: Monoclonal Interstitial Nephritis with IgA-Kappa Plasma Cells Deposition in Sjögren Syndrome: A Case Report.
items.abstract: In Sjögren syndrome, tubulointerstitial involvement is a frequent finding, characterized by lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, tubular atrophy, and interstitial fibrosis. Nevertheless, descriptions of monoclonal interstitial infiltrates remain scarce. These observations suggest that beyond the classical spectrum of glomerular or tubular injury, a subset of patients with Sjögren syndrome may present atypical renal manifestations potentially associated with underlying monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance. This highlights the importance of accurately characterizing infiltrates and carefully considering monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance (MGRS) as a potential contributor to disease heterogeneity and long-term kidney outcomes. An 83-year-old woman with Sjögren syndrome presented with a rapidly progressive decline in kidney function, without proteinuria. Immunologic and viral workup was unremarkable. A kidney biopsy revealed marked interstitial plasma cell infiltration, as demonstrated by CD138+ staining and IgA-kappa restriction by immunohistochemistry, with no glomerular involvement. Bone marrow evaluation showed <10% plasma cells, excluding multiple myeloma. Serum electrophoresis confirmed an IgA-kappa monoclonal spike and abnormal free light chain ratio. Chemotherapy with bortezomib, dexamethasone, and lenalidomide resulted in an improvement of kidney function and normalization of IgA levels. The interstitium is frequently overlooked in MGRS classification; however, interstitial monoclonal plasma cell infiltration has recently been described in a subgroup of patients with Sjögren syndrome. It may represent a novel entity within MGRS, potentially enhancing prognosis through plasma cell-directed therapies.

items.title: Quality of Care of Patients with Gout in Primary Care Settings in the Philippines.
items.abstract: Despite established treatment guidelines, variations in the management of patients with gout in primary care settings are observed, leading to suboptimal patient outcomes. This study aimed to describe the quality of care among adult patients with gout who consulted in selected urban, rural, and remote primary care sites in the Philippines. This retrospective study involved review of electronic medical records (EMR) of adult patients diagnosed with gout between 2016 and 2022 in three primary care clinics in urban, rural, and remote settings in the Philippines. Quality of care was assessed based on adherence to predefined quality indicators from recommendations of the 2016 EULAR guidelines for gout management, including lifestyle counseling, comorbidity screening, prescription of recommended anti-inflammatory agents to patients with acute gout, and urate-lowering therapy (ULT) prescription. A total of 557 patients were included in the study. The cohort was predominantly male (67.1%), with a mean age of 55.2 years. Young-onset gout (age <40 years) was present in 18.1% of patients. The remote site had the lowest rate of baseline SUA determination at only 7.7%, with no patient having follow-up SUA determination. The mean baseline SUA level was 8.8 mg/dL, with the highest baseline SUA seen at the remote site (9.6 mg/dL). Screening rates for comorbidities were also suboptimal at 2.5%. Appropriate anti-inflammatory treatment for acute gouty flares was provided in 45.6% of patients, with the lowest adherence at the rural site (17.6%). The majority (90%) of the 20 patients who were identified to have indications for ULT were prescribed ULTs. Prescription of allopurinol as first-line ULT was highest in the rural (69.1%) and remote sites (65.9%) and lowest in the urban site (36.7%). Overutilization of ULT was observed across the 3 sites (36.1%), with the highest overutilization observed in the remote (52.1%) and rural sites (34.6%). Health disparities were observed, with the remote site having the highest overutilization of non-recommended analgesics, the least frequent serum uric acid determination, and the least frequent follow-up consults. Highest overutilization of ULT was observed in the urban and remote sites. The rural site had the highest percentage of patients with severe disease and the lowest adherence to the prescription of appropriate anti-inflammatory therapy for acute gouty arthritis and screening for comorbidities. These findings reflect the need to improve gout management in primary care and highlight the need for targeted strategies appropriate according to the setting, especially in underserved populations in rural and remote areas.

items.title: Prevalence of Psoriatic Arthritis among Patients with Psoriasis Using the Psoriatic Arthritis Screening Tool (PEST) Questionnaire in a Tertiary Government Institution.
items.abstract: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a complex musculoskeletal disorder that is associated with psoriasis. Its estimated prevalence among patients with psoriasis ranges widely from 6% to 42% in Europe, North America, and South Africa. However, there is a paucity of data in Asia. To date, there is no local study done in the Philippines. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of psoriatic arthritis (PsA) among patients with psoriasis in a tertiary institution. This is a descriptive cross-sectional study that included 150 patients with psoriasis in the Dermatology Clinic. Demographic and clinical data were collected. Psoriatic Arthritis Screening Tool (PEST) was applied to all participants. Those who scored ≥3 on the PEST were seen at the Rheumatology Clinic and confirmed with the Classification of Psoriatic Arthritis (CASPAR) Criteria. Descriptive statistics were used to describe the demographic and clinical characteristics. The prevalence of psoriatic arthritis among patients with psoriasis was calculated as the percentage of the population who scored ≥3 on the CASPAR Criteria. Out of the 150 patients with psoriasis, a total of 50 scored ≥3 on PEST. Of these, 47 patients (31.3%) qualified for the diagnosis of PsA using the CASPAR criteria. Thirty-seven out of the forty-seven patients (79%) are known PsA patients, while the remaining 10 patients (21%) were newly diagnosed with PsA. A total of 34 patients (72%) were female, with a mean age of 33 and 39 years at the onset of psoriasis and PsA, respectively. Family history of psoriasis was present in 22 patients (47%). The most common pattern of arthritis was polyarticular (51%) followed by oligoarticular (38%) and axial (11%). Morning stiffness was present in 83% of the patients. Dactylitis was recorded in 16 patients (34%), while 19 patients (40%) had enthesopathy. Onycholysis was the most common nail abnormality seen in 20 patients (43%). Only 13 patients had rheumatoid factor at baseline, and all were negative. Most of the patients did not have imaging studies at baseline. In this single center study, the diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis among patients who were previously diagnosed with psoriasis increased from 24.5% to 31.3% using PEST as a screening tool, showing its usefulness in improving clinical detection of psoriatic arthritis among these patients.

items.title: Anti-Transcriptional Intermediary Factor 1 Gamma Antibody-Positive Dermatomyositis Concomitant with Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: Case Report and Literature Review.
items.abstract: Anti-transcriptional intermediary factor 1 gamma antibody-positive dermatomyositis (anti-TIF1-γ-DM) is a paraneoplastic syndrome occurring in various neoplasms, but reports elaborating on anti-TIF1-γ-DM patients accompanied by lymphoma are scarce. We report 2 patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) complicated by anti-TIF1-γ-DM and carried out TIF1-γ immunohistochemistry on tissue sections of DLBCL and skin of anti-TIF1-γ-DM patients and controls. Genetic analysis of exons 2 and 10 of TRIM33 , the gene coding TIF1-γ, was also carried out in DLBCL and skin samples of anti-TIF1-γ-DM patients and controls to look for recurrent mutations. Case 1 was a 65-year-old male and case 2 was a 52-year-old male, and both patients presented with DLBCL complicated by anti-TIF1-γ-DM. R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisolone) therapy led to remissions of both anti-TIF1-γ-DM and DLBCL in both cases. Immunohistochemistry showed strong TIF1-γ expression in DLBCL and skin samples from both patients with anti-TIF1-γ-DM and controls. Mutations in exons 2 and 10 of TRIM33 have been previously reported in DLBCL cells of an anti-TIF1-γ-DM patient, but analysis of the same exons revealed no recurrent mutations in our cases. Anti-TIF1-γ-DM very often presents with a concomitant neoplasm, and a systemic evaluation for malignancy including lymphoma is mandatory. The etiology of anti-TIF1-γ-DM in patients with lymphoma remains unknown, and the underlying mechanisms have yet to be elucidated.

items.title: Bilateral Foot Drop as the Presenting Manifestation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus-Associated Mononeuritis Multiplex: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Peripheral nervous system involvement in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is uncommon, and mononeuritis multiplex as the presenting neurological manifestation is particularly rare. Early recognition may be difficult when the initial clinical picture resembles focal compressive neuropathy. A 31-year-old previously healthy woman developed acute right foot numbness and foot drop after right knee pain and earlier nonspecific arthralgia. Initial assessments favored peroneal neurapraxia. Over the following 3 weeks, her deficits progressed to persistent right foot drop followed by new left lower limb numbness and weakness, resulting in asymmetric bilateral foot drop. Electrophysiological studies demonstrated an asymmetric, non-length-dependent motor and sensory axonal neuropathy consistent with mononeuritis multiplex. Magnetic resonance imaging of the lumbosacral spine excluded a compressive lumbosacral explanation and focused ultrasound showed no compressive lesion involving the right common peroneal nerve. Serological evaluation revealed high-titer antinuclear antibody, positive anti-double-stranded DNA, anti-Ro, anti-ribosomal P antibodies, elevated inflammatory markers, and a positive lupus anticoagulant screen, with negative infectious screening and no evidence of active lupus nephritis. She was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone, intravenous immunoglobulin, hydroxychloroquine, and rituximab, followed by oral corticosteroid tapering and rehabilitation. Her pain improved early, distal motor function partially recovered, and she later demonstrated meaningful functional improvement with orthotic and rehabilitation support. This case suggests that SLE may initially present predominantly as mononeuritis multiplex, with evolving bilateral foot drop as the dominant neurological and function-threatening manifestation, through a suspected vasculitic mechanism, even when more typical renal, serosal, or major mucocutaneous features are absent at neurological presentation. In patients with progressive or sequential foot drop, especially when the presentation becomes bilateral or multifocal, prompt electrodiagnostic testing and evaluation for systemic autoimmune disease are essential to avoid diagnostic delay and allow timely immunotherapy. Foot drop means difficulty lifting the front part of the foot, which can cause tripping or an abnormal walking pattern. It is often caused by pressure on a nerve near the knee or by a problem in the lower back. This case describes a 31-year-old woman who first developed numbness and weakness in her right foot. At first, her symptoms looked similar to a common nerve compression problem. Over the next few weeks, she developed symptoms in both legs. Nerve tests showed that several separate nerves were affected. This pattern is called mononeuritis multiplex. Blood tests also supported a new diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease in which the immune system can attack the body’s own tissues. In this patient, the nerve problem was considered most likely related to lupus-associated inflammation of the small blood vessels that supply the nerves, although this was not confirmed by nerve biopsy. She was treated with medicines to reduce immune system activity, including steroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, hydroxychloroquine, and rituximab. She also received physiotherapy and ankle-foot supports to improve walking. Her pain and movement improved, although some weakness remained during follow-up. This case highlights that worsening or bilateral foot drop should not always be assumed to be due to simple nerve compression. When symptoms progress or affect both sides, doctors should consider inflammatory and autoimmune causes and arrange appropriate nerve and blood tests.

items.title: Drug interactions in rheumatoid arthritis: a disparity between electronic database prediction and real-world co-prescription with different large language models.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disease that often requires multi-drug regimens, which can increase the risk of drug-drug interactions (DDIs). To determine whether polypharmacy contributes to potential DDIs in patients with RA. A retrospective observational study that integrates data from drug interaction databases and medical records, supplemented by artificial intelligence analysis. Twenty-one RA drugs and 54 commonly prescribed medicines were screened for potential DDIs using the Micromedex and WebMD databases and compared with real-world co-prescription at our hospital. The ChatGPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 large language models (LLMs) were also evaluated as "AI judges" versus an expert rheumatologist to assess real-world co-prescription. This study was conducted from January to September 2025. Among 75 frequently prescribed medicines in RA patients, 753 database-predicted potential DDIs were reported, with Micromedex showing 464 DDI pairs and WebMD showing 600 pairs. Both databases classified 47 serious potential DDIs as contraindicated or major, with high concordance. The main predicted DDI mechanisms were immunosuppression (27%), methotrexate toxicity (18%), and nephrotoxicity (12%), with tacrolimus (12%), methotrexate (10%), and infliximab (6%) as major culprit drugs. In real-world co-prescriptions, 259 RA patients showed methotrexate/naproxen (46.4%) and methotrexate/sulfasalazine (29.5%) as the most common real-world co-prescribing patterns with potential DDIs. Brennan-Prediger kappa values indicated fair agreement (0.3161) in the electronic database predictions and conditional agreement (0.9807) among preselected serious DDIs. The LLM evaluation revealed that advanced models (e.g., Gemini 2.5 Pro) provided finesse recommendations highly concordant with expert opinion, whereas simpler models were more conservatively aligned with database alerts. In both real-world co-prescription and database evaluation, serious potential DDIs were associated mainly with methotrexate toxicity. Based on these exploratory findings, advanced LLMs show potential to assist with the contextualizing rigid database alerts and supporting pragmatic clinical decision-making. However, expert clinical judgment and direct patient consultation remain essential to improve RA patient safety and medication adherence. Comparative drug interactions in rheumatoid arthritis patients Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a complex disease that requires multiple medications and might cause drug-drug interactions (DDIs). There is inadequate information comparing potential DDI predictions between electronic database and real-world co-prescription, especially with AI support. Our study revealed a high number of potential DDIs among medicines commonly prescribed for RA patients. Furthermore, the significant discordance in DDI predictions was detected between the electronic database and the real-world co-prescription, with large language models (LLMs). The real-world co-prescription indicated that methotrexate and NSAIDs/sulfasalazine pose a high risk for serious DDIs. By using advanced LLMs provided nuanced advice consistent with expert rheumatologist consensus by continuing treatment with careful monitoring for these serious DDIs. Management of harmful DDIs requires integrating modern decision support tools, deep clinical expertise, and direct patient communication.

items.title: Current aspects of the etiopathogenesis of antiphospholipid syndrome and its clinical manifestations.
items.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome is a systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by the persistent presence of antiphospholipid antibodies and a predisposition to arterial, venous, and microvascular thrombotic manifestations. In this article, the authors analyzed the available literature sources in the PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar databases for the period from 2019 to 2026, focusing on the epidemiological, gender-related, etiopathogenetic, clinical, and diagnostic aspects of antiphospholipid syndrome. Antiphospholipid syndrome emerges as a systemic immune-vascular nosological entity in which cerebrovascular and cardiovascular manifestations constitute the main clinical phenotype and determine the long-term prognosis of the disease. Understanding antiphospholipid syndrome as a unified immune-coagulation process is of fundamental importance for clinical practice, as it provides a basis for more accurate risk stratification, early identification of patients with a high probability of severe vascular complications, and the development of pathogenetically substantiated therapeutic methods targeting not only the coagulation cascade but also the immune and inflammatory components of the disease. Such an integrative approach is fundamental to optimizing treatment and improving the prognosis of patients with antiphospholipid syndrome.

items.title: Expression Profile of the IL-17 Receptor Family on Peripheral B Lymphocytes in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: B cells are key contributors to the immunopathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), yet the expression profile of interleukin-17 (IL-17) receptors on human B cells remains incompletely defined. We analyzed the surface expression of IL-17RA-IL-17RE on peripheral CD19 + B cells from 42 patients with RA and 20 healthy controls (HC) using flow cytometry. Receptor-positive cell frequency and mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) were evaluated, and disease activity was assessed using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints based on erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS28-ESR). The frequency of receptor-positive B cells differed significantly among IL-17 receptor (IL-17R) family members in both RA and HC, with IL-17RD showing the highest proportion of positive cells, followed by IL-17RA, whereas IL-17RC was less frequent and IL-17RB and IL-17RE were rarely detected. The proportion of IL-17RA + B cells was lower in RA than in HC and remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons (Holm-adjusted p = 0.0126). A nominally lower frequency of IL-17RC + B cells in RA did not remain significant after adjustment, while IL-17RD frequency was comparable between groups. No between-group differences in MFI remained significant after multiple-comparison correction. Receptor expression was not significantly associated with DAS28-ESR disease activity categories. These findings provide a descriptive characterization of the IL-17R family on peripheral B cells in RA and identify a lower frequency of IL-17RA + B cells as the most robust between-group difference, suggesting alterations in IL-17R dynamics that may contribute to B-cell dysregulation and disease pathogenesis.

items.title: Mosaic KRAS variants in childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Clinical targeted sequencing identified low-VAF KRAS variants in two of 26 children with childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Both had severe inflammatory manifestations but lacked Noonan syndrome features, and neither developed persistent lymphoproliferation suggestive of RAS-associated autoimmune lymphoproliferative disease during follow-up. These findings suggest that KRAS mosaicism may contribute to the development or severity of childhood-onset SLE.

items.title: A Multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program for the Evaluation and Management of Patients With SLE and Cognitive Concerns.
items.abstract: To develop and implement a standardized, comprehensive multidisciplinary program for the evaluation and management of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and cognitive concerns that would lead to improved diagnosis and management. The Neuro-Lupus Program evaluated 50 patients with SLE referred for any neurocognitive concern over a 12-month period. A specific sequential work-up protocol was developed for standardized patient evaluation. Initial history and examination were performed by a dedicated lupus neurologist followed by referral for comprehensive neurocognitive testing. Patients with suspected mood or psychotic disorders were evaluated in a specialized autoimmune psychiatry clinic. MRI brain scans were performed in all patients. Patients with MRI evidence of inflammation or cognitive impairment were further assessed with CSF studies and FDG-PET/CT brain. Management of neuropsychiatric medications and immunotherapy was a collaboration between neurology, psychiatry, and rheumatology. Full neurocognitive evaluation revealed a previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in 46.4% of patients tested (mild 39.3%, major 7.1%), with an additional 39.3% demonstrating a normal cognitive profile with isolated weakness. MRI demonstrated white matter disease in 50% of patients and cerebral atrophy in 10%. Brain FDG-PET/CT was performed in 8 patients (16%), 7 (88%) of which were abnormal. CSF studies demonstrated normal protein and white cell counts, but 25% had elevated kappa free light chains. As a result of this program, neuropsychiatric medications were optimized in 86% of patients and 8% had an escalation in immunotherapy. This multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program model brings together neurologists, psychiatrists, rheumatologists, and neuropsychologists to standardize the approach to neurocognitive symptoms in SLE. Among the patients enrolled, this program detected previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in the majority of those tested and was associated with changes in neuropsychiatric and immunotherapy management.

items.title: Incremental Predictive Value of Dynamic Platelet-to-Lymphocyte Ratio Beyond ESR and CRP for Glucocorticoid Sparing in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Multi-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: To identify independent predictors of sustained glucocorticoid (GC) sparing in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) initiating biological or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARDs), specifically we evaluated whether the longitudinal platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (ΔPLR) trajectory provides superior prognostic value compared to conventional measurements. This multicenter retrospective study analyzed 264 patients from the Taipei Medical University Clinical Research Database. Sparing success was defined as achieving predefined dose reduction targets at month 6 and maintaining stability for ≥ 12 weeks. Candidate predictors were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by multivariable logistic and Cox proportional hazards modeling. Clinical utility was assessed using "rescue rate" analysis. Sustained GC sparing was achieved by 139 (52.7%) patients. First-line b/tsDMARD initiation was the strongest predictor (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.23, p < 0.001) of GC-sparing success. Although static baseline inflammatory markers were non-predictive, every 10% reduction in 6-month ΔPLR independently increased success odds (aOR 1.05 [inverted from 0.95 per 10% increase], p = 0.009) and significantly accelerated the sparing rate (hazard ratio [HR] 1.02, p = 0.021). Conversely, concomitant nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drug use hindered success. Notably, incorporating ΔPLR into the predictive model "rescued" 16.5% of unrecognized candidates for de-escalation-patients capable of successful GC sparing who were misclassified by standard clinical models. Although static baseline inflammatory markers are nonpredictive, 6-month ΔPLR offers significant incremental prognostic value beyond conventional erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP). By identifying 16.5% of viable candidates overlooked by standard assessments, dynamic PLR monitoring offers a potential strategy to optimize precision steroid de-escalation in RA.

items.title: Bimekizumab in Chinese Patients with Active Non-Radiographic Axial Spondyloarthritis: 52-Week Results from the Phase 3 BE MOBILE 1 Study.
items.abstract: Bimekizumab, a humanised monoclonal IgG1 antibody that selectively inhibits interleukin (IL)-17F in addition to IL-17A, was efficacious and well tolerated to 52 weeks in patients with non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (nr-axSpA) in the global phase 3 multicentre study BE MOBILE 1. In this pre-specified analysis, we examine in more detail the efficacy and safety of bimekizumab in the Chinese subpopulation of patients with nr-axSpA from BE MOBILE 1. BE MOBILE 1 comprised a 16-week double-blind, placebo-controlled period and 36-week maintenance period. Patients with nr-axSpA were randomised to receive subcutaneous bimekizumab 160 mg every 4 weeks or placebo to week 16; thereafter, all patients received bimekizumab. Here we report efficacy and safety outcomes to week 52 for the Chinese subpopulation. No formal statistical comparisons were made; results should be interpreted as nominal. Overall, 36/274 patients in BE MOBILE 1 were enrolled in China (bimekizumab-randomised 18; placebo-randomised 18); 32 completed week 52. A greater proportion of bimekizumab- vs placebo-randomised patients achieved Assessment of SpondyloArthritis international Society (ASAS) ≥ 40% response (38.9% vs 22.2%), ASAS partial remission (33.3% vs 11.1%), and Axial Spondyloarthritis Disease Activity Score < 2.1 (77.7% vs 49.7%) at week 16. By week 52, improvements were comparable between bimekizumab-randomised and placebo-randomised patients who had switched to bimekizumab. Similar trends were observed for objective signs of inflammation, spinal pain, physical function, health-related quality of life, and peripheral manifestations. To week 52, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) occurred in 33 bimekizumab-treated patients (91.7%), with upper respiratory tract infection the most frequent (10 patients [27.8%]). Four patients (11.1%) had serious TEAEs; four had fungal infections (11.1%; all Tinea). No patients experienced adjudicated inflammatory bowel disease or uveitis. In patients with nr-axSpA from China, bimekizumab showed rapid and sustained efficacy improvements to week 52 and was well tolerated, consistent with the global patient population. Graphical Abstract is available for this article. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier, NCT03928704.

items.title: Comprehensive regulatory network construction highlights lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA-TF interactions and key molecular drivers in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent inflammation and progressive joint damage. Although numerous molecular contributors have been reported, the integrated regulatory architecture linking coding and non-coding transcripts remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to construct a multilayer lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA-transcription factor (TF) network to prioritize candidate regulators associated with RA. Publicly available RNA-sequencing datasets from RA and control samples were retrieved from the NCBI Sequence Read Archive. Differential expression analysis was performed using DESeq2. High-confidence miRNA-mRNA interactions were obtained from miRDip, miRNA-lncRNA associations from miRNet, and TF annotations from AnimalTFDB. Functional enrichment analyses were conducted to identify overrepresented biological themes. Network topology and module structure were evaluated in Cytoscape using CytoHubba and MCODE. Integration of interaction datasets identified 179 mRNAs targeted by 93 miRNAs, of which 90 miRNAs were connected to 404 annotated lncRNAs. Twenty-five TFs were incorporated into the regulatory framework. Degree-based analysis highlighted QKI, hsa-miR-497-5p, and KCNQ1OT1 as the most connected nodes within their respective categories. Module detection revealed five densely interconnected sub-networks, indicating coordinated regulatory organization. Several prioritized elements have previously been implicated in immune or inflammatory regulation, supporting the biological relevance of the network. This integrative analysis delineates a comprehensive regulatory landscape of RA and provides a ranked set of candidate molecules for future experimental validation. Among these, CCDC6 was identified as a downregulated gene positioned within a highly connected module and linked to multiple hub miRNAs and lncRNAs, suggesting potential functional importance in RA pathobiology.

items.title: Emerging drugs in phase 2/3 and selected phase 1/2 cellular-therapy trials: a glimpse into the future of systemic sclerosis treatment.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a complex autoimmune disease that affects multiple organs. SSc is associated with the highest mortality rate among rheumatic diseases and significantly diminishes quality of life. Consequently, research efforts have focused on understanding its etiopathogenesis and on developing related targeted therapies. Over the past decade, organ-specific therapies (such as tocilizumab and nintedanib for lung fibrosis) have been introduced to manage various manifestations of SSc. However, there is a lack of approved therapies for the overall disease. Currently, many novel compounds are being further evaluated in ongoing clinical trials. This article reviews drugs currently in phase 2 and phase 3 trials and highlights the key disease mechanisms they target in SSc. Recent advances in understanding the pathogenesis of SSc have facilitated the identification of actionable molecular and cellular pathways, leading to the testing of targeted therapeutic strategies. Concurrently, increasing emphasis is being placed on patient stratification and personalised treatment approaches to optimise clinical trial design, improve treatment responsiveness, and enhance the generalisability of trial outcomes. Among emerging treatments, cellular therapies, including chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, represent a significant innovation. This paradigm shift offers substantial potential for improving outcomes in systemic sclerosis.

items.title: Dexamethasone palmitate-loaded nanodiscs target inflamed joints and suppress rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is driven by persistent joint inflammation and dysregulated adaptive immune responses, highlighting the need for drug delivery strategies that can concentrate immunomodulatory therapy at inflamed joints and disease-associated lymphatic tissues. Here, we formulated dexamethasone palmitate-loaded synthetic high-density lipoprotein nanodiscs (DXP-NDs) as a biomimetic nanodelivery platform for subcutaneous administration and inflammation-directed delivery. DXP-NDs exhibited excellent encapsulation efficiency (95.8% ± 2.4%) and maintained their ~10 nm size for 60 days during storage either at 4 °C or 37 °C. DXP-NDs downregulated MHC-II and costimulatory molecules (CD40/CD80/CD86) on bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDCs) in vitro. In the absence of a strong antigenic signal, this costimulatory blockade significantly promoted regulatory T cell (Treg) differentiation. In contrast, upon strong antigen exposure, DXP-NDs aborted productive T-cell activation, suppressing proliferation and locking T cells in an unactivated, anergic state. Following subcutaneous administration, DiR-labeled nanodiscs selectively accumulated in inflamed joints in both zymosan-induced arthritis and collagen-induced arthritis models, with joint fluorescence correlating strongly with clinical paw scores. In a murine model of zymosan-induced arthritis, DXP-NDs alleviated inflammatory joint swelling and reduced regional Th1 frequencies. In a murine model of collagen-induced arthritis, DXP-ND therapy arrested clinical disease progression and reduced systemic IL-1β levels, with additional evidence of immune remodeling in draining lymph nodes. T-cell analysis revealed reduced Th1 and Th17 frequencies, decreased effector memory T-cell populations, and increased regulatory T-cell frequencies after extended treatment. Overall, these studies demonstrate that DXP-NDs traffic to inflamed arthritic joints and lymphatic tissues after subcutaneous administration and promote coordinated anti-inflammatory and immunoregulatory effects that attenuate joint inflammation and limit disease progression in murine arthritis models.

items.title: Predicting Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis in Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy-associated Interstitial Lung Disease: A Machine Learning Approach Integrating Quantitative CT and Clinical Features.
items.abstract: The prognosis of progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) in idiopathic inflammatory myopathy-associated interstitial lung disease (IIM-ILD) is poor, and current strategies for predicting its development are limited. This study aimed to use machine learning to integrate quantitative computed tomography (QCT) and clinical features to predict PPF in patients with IIM-ILD. We retrospectively included 180 IIM-ILD patients, of whom 86 developed PPF. We randomly assigned patients to training and validation sets in a 7:3 ratio. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and univariate analysis were employed to select the most predictive features. We independently trained 8 machine learning algorithms. Model performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curves, area under the curve (AUC) values, and decision curve analysis. 16 key clinical features and 7 QCT variables were selected for model development. The 10 variables with the highest contribution values were subsequently selected for the PPF prediction model. The clinical variables included Krebs von den Lungen-6, interleukin-6, percent-predicted forced expiratory volume in 1 second, carcinoembryonic antigen, ferritin, CD3 + T cells, natural killer cells, and CD19 + B cells. The QCT signatures included ILD Honeycomb Volume (%) Lt Lower + Rt Lower and ILD Consolidation Volume (%) Whole Lung. Among the 8 machine learning algorithms, the Random Forest model demonstrated the best predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.821 (95% CI: 0.680-0.925) in the training cohort and 0.943 (95% CI: 0.866-0.982) in the validation cohort. The integration of QCT and clinical features using machine learning offers a potential non-invasive approach for predicting PPF in patients with IIM-ILD. This strategy may facilitate the early identification of individuals at high risk of PPF and potentially support timely clinical intervention.

items.title: Radiographic patellofemoral differences between end-stage knee rheumatoid arthritis and matched knee osteoarthritis vary by arithmetic hip-knee-ankle-angle-defined coronal alignment.
items.abstract: To compare radiographic patellofemoral phenotypes between end-stage knee rheumatoid arthritis (KRA) and matched knee osteoarthritis (KOA), assess disease type by coronal alignment interactions, and characterize within-KRA variation by alignment and patella baja. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 669 KRA and 669 KOA knees undergoing total knee arthroplasty from 2001 to 2024. After 1:1 propensity score matching for age, sex, and body mass index, 542 matched pairs were analyzed. Patellofemoral parameters were measured on standardized lateral and skyline radiographs. Paired tests, generalized estimating equations, nonparametric tests, and adjusted regression were used. Patella baja was more prevalent in KRA than KOA (matched-pair odds ratio, 7.03; 95% confidence interval, 5.00-9.87), and Wiberg type III radiographic appearance was more frequent (39.5% vs. 11.3%; P < 0.001). KRA also showed lower Insall-Salvati index and higher lateral patellar displacement rate. All eight KRA-KOA differences remained significant in alignment-adjusted and Larsen grade 4-5-restricted sensitivity analyses (all P < 0.001). Significant disease type-by-alignment interactions were observed for Wiberg score, lateral patellar displacement rate, lateral patellar tilt angle, lateral patellar angle, and congruence angle. Differences in displacement, tilt, and congruence were greatest in valgus knees. Within KRA, Wiberg type III was more frequent in varus and valgus than neutral knees and increased across Larsen grades; within-alignment associations with patella baja were limited and non-uniform. End-stage KRA showed a distinct radiographic patellofemoral phenotype compared with matched KOA, with several between-disease differences varying by coronal alignment.

items.title: Population Pharmacokinetics of Intravenous and Subcutaneous Belimumab, and Clinical Response Prediction in Chinese Pediatric Patients with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: Intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC) belimumab are approved in the USA, Europe, and Japan for patients aged ≥ 5 years with active systemic lupus erythematosus. In China, IV belimumab is approved for patients aged ≥ 5 years. This analysis updates the global pediatric population pharmacokinetic model by integrating data from IV and SC Chinese pediatric studies and evaluates the suitability of a 200-mg SC dosing regimen for pediatric systemic lupus erythematosus in China. This analysis utilized the previously established two-compartment model while re-evaluating the impact of potential covariates. Allometric scaling was incorporated to account for variations in body size, and other covariates were systematically assessed through stepwise selection and their relevance to pharmacokinetic parameters. To support extrapolation of the established efficacy from the IV belimumab pediatric study to SC belimumab in pediatric patients, simulations were conducted to compare pharmacokinetic exposures between the proposed SC and approved IV regimens in Chinese pediatric patients. Furthermore, to provide additional evidence for supporting dose selection in this population, clinical response was predicted using a pre-established exposure-response model. The estimated pharmacokinetic parameters for a representative Chinese pediatric patient were: clearance, 158 mL/day; steady-state volume of distribution, 3930 mL; SC bioavailability, 77.9%. Identified significant covariates included body weight (influencing clearance and volume of distribution), and baseline immunoglobulin G and albumin levels (affecting clearance). A systematic bias of -34% in drug concentrations was observed in Chinese versus global studies. This discrepancy is unlikely to stem from racial or physiological differences and may instead be attributed to study operational factors. The established exposure-response model confirmed that simulated exposures for IV and SC regimens in Chinese pediatric patients reached the plateau of the exposure-response curve. Further simulations demonstrated that both the two-weight-band SC regimen and the trial-studied three-weight-band regimen produced exposures comparable to the IV regimen in Chinese pediatric patients. This analysis supports the suitability of a two-weight-band, dosing interval-adjusted 200-mg SC regimen for Chinese pediatric patients with systemic lupus erythematosus. Compared with the three-weight-band regimen, the two-weight-band approach simplifies administration and enhances feasibility for clinical implementation. Belimumab treats systemic lupus erythematosus, a disease where the immune system attacks the body’s own tissues. While children in many countries can receive belimumab as either an intravenous infusion or a subcutaneous injection, only the intravenous form is approved for pediatric use in China. This study investigated whether Chinese children with systemic lupus erythematosus could safely and effectively use the subcutaneous form, and what the best dosing schedule would be.This study combined data from Chinese and non-Chinese children who received intravenous or subcutaneous belimumab. A mathematical model was updated to track how the drug moves through the body, and the influence of factors like body weight and blood protein levels (immunoglobulin G and albumin) was analyzed. Computer simulations compared different dosing schedules and predicted their effectiveness based on established links between drug exposure and clinical response.The results showed that a child’s weight, immunoglobulin G, and albumin levels were the main factors influencing how much belimumab stayed in the body. Chinese children had about 34% lower drug concentrations than non-Chinese children, a difference likely due to study procedures rather than biology. Simulations found that giving subcutaneous injections once a week for children weighing 40 kg or more, and once every 2 weeks for those between 15 and 40 kg, would achieve drug levels similar to the approved intravenous treatment. This study supports this simpler two-group dosing approach for Chinese children with systemic lupus erythematosus, which is expected to be as effective as intravenous treatment and more convenient for patients and healthcare providers.

items.title: Prevalence of Urinary Incontinence and Associated Factors in Women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) can compromise the pelvic floor muscles, with the possible occurrence of urinary incontinence (UI). This study aimed to determine the prevalence of UI and associated factors in women with SLE. A cross-sectional study was conducted over 12 months in women with SLE. UI was assessed using the three Incontinence Questions (3IQ), severity using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire - Short Form (ICIQ-SF), impact of urinary symptoms using the Urinary Impact Questionnaire (UIQ-7), quality of life (QoL) using the 12-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-12), and functional performance using the 30-s Sit-to-Stand (SIT) and Timed Up and Go (TUG) tests. Descriptive and bivariate analyses were performed, and factors associated with urinary incontinence (UI) were investigated using Poisson regression with robust variance, with prevalence ratios (PR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05. A total of 231 women (age 47 ± 12 years) were included. UI was identified in 52% (95% CI 46.0-58.7) of the participants. In the bivariate analysis, UI was associated with age, paid employment, family income, and some clinical and obstetric characteristics. In the final multivariate Poisson regression model, lower physical and mental health scores were associated with UI (PCS PR 0.99; 95% CI 0.97-1.00; p = 0.024; MCS PR 0.99; 95% CI 0.97-1.00; p = 0.033). UI was present in more than half of the women with SLE and was associated with worse QoL.

items.title: Latent class analysis of CT-based phenotypes in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis and pulmonary involvement.
items.abstract: Pulmonary manifestations of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) are highly heterogeneous, and a standardized CT-based classification is currently lacking. This study aimed to evaluate whether latent class analysis (LCA) of chest CT findings can identify phenotypes with clinical and prognostic relevance in patients with EGPA. We retrospectively enrolled 140 patients with EGPA and pulmonary involvement between 2014 and 2025. Chest CT findings were independently evaluated by two thoracic radiologists and analyzed using LCA to identify CT-based phenotypes. Reproducibility and clinical applicability were assessed by having radiologists reassign patients to phenotypes based on LCA-derived CT patterns while blinded to the original LCA assignments. Baseline characteristics and one-year clinical and radiological outcomes were compared across phenotypes. Modified Poisson regression was used to assess clinical relapse risk. LCA identified four distinct phenotypes: bronchial (32.1%; airway-predominant abnormalities), infiltrative (20.7%; parenchyma-predominant abnormalities), mixed (14.3%; combined bronchial and infiltrative features), and nonspecific (32.9%; without a dominant bronchial or infiltrative pattern). The bronchial and infiltrative phenotypes showed more favorable short-term outcomes, whereas the nonspecific phenotype mainly showed stable outcomes. The mixed phenotype remained associated with a higher risk of one-year clinical relapse after adjustment for age, sex, and baseline treatment. Radiologist reassignment showed excellent inter- and intra-observer agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.85 and 0.87). LCA enables the identification of CT-based phenotypes with distinct clinical characteristics and short-term outcome patterns in EGPA, suggesting potential prognostic value and a practical role in clinical management. QuestionCan latent class analysis (LCA) of chest CT findings identify imaging phenotypes of pulmonary involvement in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA)? FindingsLCA identified four CT-based phenotypes (bronchial, infiltrative, mixed, and nonspecific), each characterized by distinct clinical and radiological features and short-term outcome patterns. Clinical relevanceCT-based phenotyping may help characterize pulmonary disease heterogeneity in EGPA and identify patients, particularly those with the mixed phenotype, who may require closer monitoring for clinical relapse.

items.title: Impact of pregnancy on organ damage in systemic lupus erythematosus: a multicentre study.
items.abstract: Pregnancy in SLE is associated with increased maternal and fetal risks but its impact on irreversible organ damage remains unclear. We assessed whether pregnancy independently contributes to short-term organ damage accrual in women with SLE. We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from two tertiary referral centres with dedicated pregnancy clinics. Women fulfilling SLE classification criteria were included if complete damage assessments were available from 2 years before conception to 1 year after conception. Organ damage was assessed using the Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics Damage Index (SDI). Within-patient SDI changes during the pregnancy/early postpartum period were compared with the pre-pregnancy reference period. Given the limited number of events, effect sizes and CIs were prioritised. Sensitivity analyses included non-parametric effect sizes and restriction to one pregnancy per woman. 165 pregnancies were included. At conception, most women were in remission or low disease activity. During pregnancy, 20.6% experienced disease flares, predominantly mild to moderate. Overall, cumulative damage remained stable: mean SDI increased from 0.18±0.43 one year before conception to 0.22±0.52 one year after conception (mean ΔSDI 0.04±0.21), with a median change of zero. Only seven pregnancies (4.2%; 95% CI 2.1% to 8.5%) showed new damage, limited to a single SDI item. Pre-existing damage was associated with progression (OR 6.77; 95% CI 1.43 to 32.05), and the frequency of progression was similar when the analyses were restricted to a single pregnancy per woman (6/126, 4.8%). By contrast, disease activity at the time of conception, flare-ups, obstetric complications and treatments were inconclusive. In the sensitivity analysis, the association with pre-existing damage was confirmed, and baseline disease activity also emerged as associated with damage progression (rank-biserial r=−0.55; 95% CI −0.78 to −0.27, p=0.030). In women with predominantly well-controlled SLE, short-term organ damage accrual during pregnancy and the early postpartum period was uncommon. Pre-existing damage was associated with further accrual, while baseline disease activity also emerged as associated in the sensitivity analysis; however, the small number of events limits conclusions regarding other potential risk factors.

items.title: Type I interferon activation in classical monocytes and GZMK+ CD8+ T cells characterises the ultrasound-negative phase of imminent rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a prototypical autoimmune disease, characterised by prolonged systemic autoimmunity before organ-specific tissue inflammation. Understanding immune mechanisms that drive the transition from systemic autoimmunity to joint-specific pathology is key to arthritis prevention. In this study, we define immune signatures in anticitrullinated protein antibodies-positive (ACPA+) at-risk individuals who imminently progress to RA, comparing those with and without ultrasound (US)-detectable subclinical synovitis. We performed single‑cell RNA sequencing and proteomic profiling on prospectively collected blood samples from high-risk ACPA+ imminent progressors (n = 22), who were further stratified by the presence or absence of US-detectable subclinical synovitis and compared them with ACPA+ nonprogressors (n=18). We found type I interferon (IFN-I) upregulation in peripheral CD14+ classical monocyte and Granzyme K protein (GZMK)+ CD8+ T cells in US-negative (USneg, n = 11) imminent progressors. In contrast, US-positive (USpos, n = 11) progressors exhibited a phenotypic shift in CD14+ classical monocytes towards interleukin 1 beta (IL1ß)+ expression and clonal expansion of GZMB+ cytotoxic CD8+ T cells. GZMB+ and GZMK+ CD8+ T cells were largely clonotypically distinct. Plasma proteomics also revealed a shift from Toll-like receptor-associated innate pathways in USneg progressors towards effector and tissue-remodelling signatures in USpos progressors. In ACPA+ high-risk individuals, IFN-I-driven activation of peripheral innate CD14+ classical monocytes and GZMK+ CD8+ T cell subsets occur before the onset of subclinical synovitis when RA is imminent. Distinct inflammatory and effector programmes, including GZMB+ CD8+ T cells clonal expansion, are associated with the onset of subclinical synovitis.

items.title: Macrophage-derived secretory Clusterin amplifies fibroblast-like synoviocyte activation through PI3K/AKT and NF-κB signaling in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Secretory clusterin (sCLU) has been implicated in inflammatory diseases, yet its role in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains poorly defined. Here, we showed that serum sCLU levels were significantly elevated in patients with RA compared with healthy controls (n = 192 RA; n = 139 HC) and were associated with disease activity. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate diagnostic performance for RA discrimination (AUC = 0.783, 95% CI 0.730-0.837). Mechanistically, M1-polarized macrophages exhibited enhanced sCLU secretion, whereas RA fibroblast-like synoviocytes (RA-FLS) produced minimal sCLU, identifying inflammatory macrophages as an important source of extracellular sCLU. Using a Transwell co-culture system and recombinant sCLU stimulation, we found that sCLU amplified inflammatory cytokine production and promoted the proliferative, migratory, invasive, and apoptosis-resistant phenotypes of RA-FLS under inflammatory conditions. These effects were accompanied with activation of the PI3K/AKT and NF-κB pathways and were significantly attenuated by pharmacological inhibition of either pathway. Proteomic screening, surface plasmon resonance, and co-immunoprecipitation analyses identified fibronectin 1 (FN1) as a direct binding partner of sCLU although its functional contribution requires further investigation. Importantly, genetic deletion of sCLU alleviated disease severity in collagen-induced arthritis mice. Collectively, our findings identify macrophage-derived sCLU as an inflammatory amplifier in RA and suggest that targeting sCLU may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for inflammatory arthritis.

items.title: Real-world comparison of jak inhibitors and TNF inhibitor cycling in axial spondyloarthritis patients after TNFi failure.
items.abstract: This study compared drug survival and clinical outcomes between tumor necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) cycling and switching to a Janus kinase inhibitor (JAKi) in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) patients after initial TNFi failure. This retrospective longitudinal observational cohort study included 123 axSpA patients fulfilling the Assessment of SpondyloArthritis International Society (ASAS) criteria, followed in a tertiary rheumatology clinic. After failure of the first TNFi, patients were directed to either a second TNFi or a JAKi based on clinical evaluation. Notably, JAKi therapy was considered for patients with inadequate response to one or two prior TNFi agents. Drug survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and group comparisons were made using the log-rank test. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly shorter drug survival in the JAKi group compared to the TNFi group ( p  < 0.001). In the TNFi group, higher CRP levels were associated with prolonged drug survival (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.83-0.99; p  = 0.035), while primary non-response to the first TNFi predicted earlier discontinuation of the second TNFi (HR: 2.1; 95% CI: 1.08-3.14; p  = 0.033). In the JAKi group, prior failure of two different TNFi agents was associated with a lower risk of discontinuation (HR: 0.04; 95% CI: 0.01-0.39; p  = 0.007). Following prior TNFi failure, TNFi cycling was associated with longer observed drug survival compared with JAKi therapy. However, given the retrospective design and differences in prior treatment exposure, this finding should be interpreted as a descriptive real-world observation rather than definitive evidence of comparative effectiveness. JAK inhibitors may still represent a viable option for selected refractory patients with multiple prior TNFi failures.

items.title: Network pharmacology-guided investigation of the anti-angiogenic mechanisms of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn stem in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a severe systemic autoimmune disease characterized by progressive joint destruction. Spatholobi Caulis (SC), derived from the vine stem of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn, has a long history of clinical application in traditional Chinese medicine for activating blood circulation and relieving rheumatic arthralgia. However, its pharmacological material basis and anti-angiogenic mechanisms for treating RA remain insufficiently elucidated. To systematically investigate the active constituents of SC and elucidate its anti-angiogenic mechanisms in RA using an integrated approach combining chemical profiling, network pharmacology, and in vivo experimental validation. The chemical profile of SC was characterized using HPLC-QE-MS. A network pharmacology approach-incorporating target screening, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, and GO/KEGG enrichment-was utilized to predict core targets and pathways. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) were performed to evaluate the binding stability between key active compounds and hub targets. Finally, the anti-arthritic and anti-angiogenic effects were validated in a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rat model using micro-CT, H&E, immunohistochemistry (CD31), ELISA, and Western blot analysis. Additionally, to directly verify the predicted interactions, the effects of the core compound 7,3',4'-trihydroxyisoflavone (THIF) on TNF-α-induced MH7A cells were assessed. Cell proliferation, VEGF secretion, migration, and protein expression of EGFR and PIK3CB were evaluated after 24 h treatment with THIF. HPLC-QE-MS identified 24 active ingredients in SC. Network analysis identified key hub targets including SRC, PIK3CB, AKT1, EGFR, and ESR1 and revealed that SC predominantly modulates the PI3K/AKT, HIF-1α, and VEGF signaling pathways. Molecular docking, MD simulations and SPR demonstrated strong binding affinities and high structural stability between core compounds (e.g., THIF, Hesperetin, Afzelechin, (-)-Maackiain) and key hub targets (e.g., PIK3CB, EGFR, ESR1). In vivo, SC administration significantly alleviated joint swelling, preserved bone morphology (increased BV/TV and BMD via micro-CT), and reduced the organ indices of the thymus and spleen. Crucially, SC remarkably suppressed synovial neovascularization (decreased CD31-positive vessels), downregulated systemic inflammatory and angiogenic cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, VEGF, TGF-α), and significantly inhibited the protein expression of SRC, STAT3, EGFR, PI3K, AKT, and HIF-1α in synovial tissues. In vitro experiments demonstrated that SC effectively inhibits the proliferation of MH7A cells. Flow cytometry analysis confirmed that SC significantly induces apoptosis in MH7A cells; However, this pro-apoptotic effect was alleviated upon addition of the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Further in vitro validation with the pure compound THIF showed that it dose-dependently suppressed TNF-α-induced MH7A cell proliferation, reduced VEGF secretion from 292.18 to 80.32 pg/mL, and inhibited cell migration. Western blot analysis confirmed that THIF significantly downregulated the protein expression of EGFR and PIK3CB in a dose-dependent manner, directly validating the SPR binding results and demonstrating targeted inhibition of the downstream pathological signaling pathways associated with RA. SC effectively ameliorates RA progression by mitigating synovial inflammation and preventing structural joint damage. Its therapeutic efficacy is primarily driven by the suppression of pathological angiogenesis via the targeted dual-inhibition of the EGFR/PI3K/AKT/HIF-1α signaling axes.

items.title: An LLM-based decision aid for collaborative decision-making in juvenile idiopathic arthritis: A multimethod evaluation.
items.abstract: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) is the most common pediatric chronic inflammatory rheumatic condition, with substantial quality-of-life impacts. Treatment selection is complex due to limited guideline evidence, and difficult trade-offs. Decisions are often solely physician driven. We evaluated the feasibility of Large Language Model-based Decision Aid (LLM-DA) designed to support collaborative rather than solely physician decision-making in JIA care. A multi-method feasibility study was conducted in accordance with the TRIPOD-LLM checklist. The aims were twofold: first, to assess the quality of the LLM-DA (OpenAI's o3 model) based on evaluations from three pediatric rheumatologists and an exploratory assessment by an LLM-as-a-Judge (OpenAI's GPT-5 model); and second, to characterize perceived value of the tool from the patient perspective through a mixed methods evaluation (n = 34). For 10 de-identified use cases, rheumatologists and LLM-Judge generated treatment recommendations and scored the LLM-DA outputs on safety, factual consistency, treatment appropriateness, and preference acknowledgment. Rheumatologists rated 97% of outputs as acceptable for safety and preference acknowledgment, 60% for factual consistency, 70% for appropriateness. Treatment recommendation agreement among all evaluators and real-world data was low at <30%. Inter-rater agreement for scores among rheumatologists was almost perfect for safety and preference acknowledgement, moderate for treatment appropriateness, and poor for factual consistency, and remained the same or improved with LLM-as-a-Judge. Variability in evaluator scoring and treatment recommendations may reflect the inherent heterogeneity in acceptable JIA treatment pathways and potential limitations in the LLM-DA's decision-making logic. Five patient themes were identified: the tool complements rheumatologist expertise, prepares patients through reflection and actionable information, builds confidence for self-advocacy, has variable value depending on the patient-physician relationship, and has potential for broader JIA self-management. These exploratory findings provide a proof-of-concept for using AI to support collaborative decision-making, while highlighting the need for future studies to determine whether LLMs can reliably support clinical practice.

items.title: Rituximab vs Azathioprine for Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis Maintenance Therapy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract: For patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), guidelines recommend considering maintenance therapy after achieving remission. Data comparing maintenance therapeutic options are limited. To compare the effects of rituximab and azathioprine maintenance therapies on remission duration for patients with EGPA who recently achieved remission of vasculitis after standard therapy, including prednisone tapering or withdrawal. From March 7, 2018, to June 2, 2022, this double-blind, double-dummy, investigator-initiated, superiority, randomized clinical trial enrolled 98 participants with EGPA from 36 hospitals in France. Inclusion eligibility required a new EGPA diagnosis or relapsing EGPA within 30 to 360 days of achieving vasculitis remission (Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 [range, 0-63, with higher scores indicating more severe disease activity]) after a standard induction regimen. Data were analyzed from April 1, 2025, to September 17, 2025. Additional analyses ended June 22, 2026. Participants were randomized to receive a predefined standardized tapering of oral prednisone and either 500 mg of intravenous rituximab every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine placebo for 24 months (n = 49) or rituximab placebo every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine for 24 months (n = 49). The primary efficacy end point was the duration of total remission during the 28-month study period while taking 7.5 mg/d or less of prednisone. The 14 secondary end points included proportion of participants remaining in remission, rate of vasculitis relapse, and rate of asthma or rhinosinusitis exacerbations. All 98 randomized participants (mean age, 59.0 years [SD, 14.4]; 50 women [51%]) received at least 1 dose of the trial regimen and 92 (94%) completed the trial. The mean time in remission with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 91.1 weeks (95% CI, 80.9-101.2) vs 96.0 weeks (95% CI, 85.6-106.5) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively (P = .38). The proportion of participants who remained in remission during the 28-month study period with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 17 of 49 (34.7%) vs 11 of 49 (22.4%; relative risk, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.83-2.73; P = .18) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively. The proportion of participants with at least 1 vasculitis relapse was 7 (14.3%) vs 9 (18.4%) in the rituximab vs azathioprine groups, respectively, and for those with at least 1 clinically significant asthma exacerbation, rhinosinusitis exacerbation, or both, it was 16 (32.7%) vs 19 (38.8%). One participant in the azathioprine group died of SARS-CoV-2 infection before vaccine development. Rituximab recipients experienced a higher incidence of severe infections (23 [46.9%] vs 12 [24.5%], respectively), primarily due to severe SARS-CoV-2 infections. For participants with newly diagnosed or relapsing EGPA, rituximab was not superior to azathioprine for improving the duration of total remission during 28 months while taking prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less.
