items.title: Rarely involved and high damage-burden joints in juvenile idiopathic arthritis: insights from the elbow, temporomandibular joint, cervical spine, hip, and shoulder.
items.abstract: The purpose of this study is to characterize clinical features, treatment patterns, and outcomes of rare and/or high damage-burden joints in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA). Patients diagnosed with JIA between January 2008 and June 2025 were included in this retrospective study. Joints involved in less than 10% of the cohort were defined as "rarely involved," and joints contributing to the total JADI-A score of the cohort were defined as "high damage-burden" joints. Among 155 patients included, temporomandibular joint (TMJ) (7.7%), cervical spine (3.9%), and shoulder (1.9%) were defined as rarely involved joints. The joints contributing most to the total JADI-A score of the cohort, including TMJ (29%), elbow (29%), and hip (19.4%), were defined as high damage-burden joints. Polyarticular disease course was the most common pattern for elbow and TMJ involvement, whereas enthesitis-related arthritis was common for hip involvement. Patients with either one of these five involvements experienced more extensive involvement, more frequent articular relapses, and higher disease activity, frequent use of bDMARDs, and rarely achieved remission off medication (ROM) (p < 0.05). Polyarticular disease course and higher ESR at diagnosis were associated with higher odds of high damage-burden joint involvement (p < 0.05).  Elbow, hip, TMJ, cervical spine, and shoulder are rare and/or high damage-burden joints of JIA. These joint involvements seem to relate to higher disease activity, more extensive disease, arthritis relapses, frequent use of bDMARDs, rare achievement of ROM, and a risk for joint damage. More extensive inflammatory disease may predispose to involvement of rare and/or high damage-burden joints. • Advances in the treatment of JIA, particularly the more widespread use of biologics, have led to significant improvements in long-term outcomes. • Suboptimal results are still encountered in JIA patients, even in the "biologic era." • Temporomandibular joint (TMJ), cervical spine, and shoulder are among the least frequently involved joints in JIA, while TMJ, elbow, and hip are associated with a high damage burden. • These five joints seem to relate to higher disease activity, more extensive disease, articular relapses, frequent use of biologic agents, rare achievement of remission off medication, and a risk of joint damage.

items.title: Compartment-specific skeletal involvement in systemic sclerosis characterized by peripheral QCT and serum osteoimmune mediators: a case-control study.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is associated with increased bone fragility, yet early, compartment-specific alterations and their osteoimmunological correlates remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to assess bone status in SSc using dual X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) complemented by peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT), and to evaluate their associations with a targeted osteoimmunological biomarker panel and clinical risk scores. This prospective cross-sectional study included 40 women with SSc (disease duration ≤ 7 years from diagnosis) and 45 non-immune female controls, frequency-matched by age. Bone status was assessed by DXA (lumbar spine, femoral neck) and distal radius pQCT. Serum levels of routine bone and mineral metabolism markers, alongside a targeted panel of osteoimmunological mediators (OPG, OPN, PDGF-BB, ACP5, RANKL, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, DKK-1) using multiplex immunoassay were measured. FRAX scores were calculated to contextualize clinical fracture risk. With broadly comparable DXA-defined bone status, pQCT revealed significantly lower trabecular volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) in SSc, while total and cortical+subcortical vBMD were comparable. Routine biochemical markers showed substantial overlap between groups, whereas SSc patients exhibited a distinct osteoimmune profile with significantly elevated OPG, ACP5, RANKL, PDGF-BB, IL-6, IL-1β, DKK-1, and RANKL/OPG after FDR correction. Exploratory biomarker-bone associations did not remain significant after correction for multiple testing. In women with relatively early SSc, pQCT identified compartment-specific differences, particularly within the trabecular compartment, despite comparable DXA-defined bone status. A distinct osteoimmunological biomarker profile was also observed in SSc, providing complementary information on disease-related skeletal alterations, while specific biomarker-bone associations require further confirmation.

items.title: Effectiveness of tocilizumab monotherapy for IgG4-related disease-like features caused by idiopathic multicentric Castleman's disease: a case-based review.
items.abstract: Idiopathic multicentric Castleman's disease (iMCD) and immunoglobulin G4-related disease (IgG4-RD) are distinct systemic inflammatory diseases that can exhibit overlapping clinical manifestations, including elevated serum IgG4 levels and tissue infiltration of IgG4-positive plasma cells. Although interleukin-6 (IL-6) inhibitors are established first-line therapies for iMCD, optimal treatment strategies for cases of iMCD with IgG4-RD-like features remain unestablished, particularly regarding whether glucocorticoids are essential or not. Herein, we report our case of iMCD with IgG4-RD-like features successfully treated with tocilizumab monotherapy. A 68-year-old female presented with dyspnea due to a recurrent laryngeal tumor, accompanied by pulmonary consolidation, mediastinal and axillary lymphadenopathy, sclerosing mesenteritis, and retroperitoneal fibrosis. Laboratory evaluation revealed elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and serum IgG4 levels. Although the organ involvement and elevated IgG4 levels were suggestive of IgG4-RD, and laryngeal and pulmonary specimens exhibited IgG4-positive plasma cell infiltration, histopathological examination of lymph node confirmed the diagnosis of iMCD; therefore, we diagnosed the patient with iMCD with IgG4-RD-like features. Tocilizumab monotherapy achieved rapid normalization of CRP and IgG4 levels, along with improvement of organ involvements. The patient attained long-term clinical remission without glucocorticoids. Our literature review identified 9 previously reported cases of iMCD with IgG4-RD-like features. Eight of nine cases showed an insufficient response to initial glucocorticoid monotherapy and subsequently required the addition of IL-6 targeting agents to obtain disease resolution. Together with the findings from our literature review, our case suggests that tocilizumab monotherapy may be a potential treatment option for IgG4-RD-like features caused by iMCD.

items.title: Computational Prediction of the Therapeutic Mechanisms From the Turmeric-Pueraria-Coix Seed Botanical Formula in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is characterized by progressive synovial inflammation and immune-metabolic reprogramming. The polyphenol-rich Turmeric-Pueraria-Coix seed (TPC) formula shows therapeutic potential against RA, though its multi-target mechanisms remain uncharacterized. To explore how TPC modulates ferroptosis and oxidative stress in RA, we integrated systems nutrition network analysis with multicohort transcriptomic datasets to identify candidate targets. Ensemble machine learning algorithms and independent cohort validation prioritized key biomarkers. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations evaluated the dynamic behavior and interaction persistence of polyphenol-target complexes, and single-cell in silico overexpression and knockout analyses characterized the regulatory consequences of perturbing these targets within RA synovial networks. Analysis identified 85 bioactive phytochemicals in the TPC formula, forming a polyphenol-dominant matrix mapping to 40 RA targets. Algorithmic and cross-cohort prioritization isolated six core genes (ALOX5, CD38, CDK1, EZH2, MAPK8, and PTGS2) linked to RA synovial transcriptomic patterns, with varying predictive performance across external cohorts. SHAP analysis highlighted PTGS2, CD38, and MAPK8; however, MD simulations prioritized CD38 and MAPK8 as stable targets of coumestrol, whereas PTGS2 exhibited less dynamic stability. Single-cell perturbation analysis revealed similar regulatory responses following MAPK8 and PTGS2 modulation, whereas CD38 knockout produced a distinct network response. These findings link TPC-derived polyphenols to CD38/MAPK8 signaling and ferroptosis in RA, providing testable molecular hypotheses for experimental validation.

items.title: Host-driven citrullination of extracellular vesicle-derived microbial proteins links P orphyromonas gingivalis to rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is closely linked to citrullinated antigens and HLA-DRB1 risk alleles, yet the origin of immunogenic citrullinated peptides remains incompletely understood. While Porphyromonas gingivalis has been implicated in RA through its bacterial peptidylarginine deiminase (PPAD), previous studies using PPAD-deficient P. gingivalis in mouse RA models reported that PPAD deletion did not attenuate disease development, suggesting the existence of additional RA-promoting mechanisms. Here, we computationally evaluate a complementary mechanism in which host peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PADI4) may modify P. gingivalis -derived proteins, generating microbial neoantigens with preferential presentation by RA-associated HLA alleles. We developed a computational framework integrating known PADI4 and PPAD substrate preferences with MHC-II antigen presentation prediction. Human proteins were first stratified based on their susceptibility to PADI4 and/or PPAD-mediated citrullination, and their presentation profiles across RA risk-associated (HLA-DRB1*04:01 and 04:04) and protective (HLA-DRB1 * 13:01 and 13:02)alleles were analyzed through MHC-II binding prediction. This analysis revealed distinct presentation signatures, including (a) global risk enrichment, (b) high-affinity binding bias, (c) characteristic allelic presentation ratios. Application of these three features led to the identification of five candidate proteins with potential relevance to RA risk, including gingipain R1 and four outer membrane proteins. These findings propose a hypothesis that host PADI4-mediated citrullination of P. gingivalis proteins may represent an additional mechanism contributing to P. gingivalis -associated acceleration of RA pathogenesis.

items.title: Oral mucous membrane pemphigoid as a window to systemic autoimmunity: two cases associated with rheumatoid arthritis and Sjögren's disease.
items.abstract: Mucous membrane pemphigoid is a rare chronic autoimmune bullous disease that predominantly affects mucosal surfaces and may lead to significant morbidity when diagnosis is delayed. Increasing evidence suggests that oral manifestations may serve as reliable early indicators of systemic immune dysregulation and can precede the recognition of other autoimmune disorders. We report two cases of oral mucous membrane pemphigoid associated with systemic autoimmune diseases, emphasizing that the oral cavity is a sentinel site for systemic autoimmunity and highlighting the importance of integrated diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. In the first case, a 68-year-old woman with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis presented with recurrent oral ulcerations that were histopathologically confirmed as mucous membrane pemphigoid. During follow-up, ocular involvement was identified as peripheral ulcerative keratitis related to rheumatoid arthritis, requiring adjustment of systemic immunosuppressive therapy. Switching to B-cell depletion therapy with rituximab resulted in the control of both the extra-articular rheumatoid arthritis manifestation and mucous membrane pemphigoid activity. In the second case, a 44-year-old woman presented with desquamative gingivitis and oral bullous lesions. After a biopsy confirmed mucous membrane pemphigoid, progressive sicca symptoms prompted rheumatological investigation, leading to the diagnosis of Sjögren's disease based on serology, imaging, and minor salivary gland biopsy. Treatment with azathioprine resulted in the clinical stabilization of both diseases. These cases illustrate how oral lesions may reveal or precede systemic autoimmune disease and underscore the diagnostic challenges of overlapping immune-mediated rheumatic diseases. Recognizing shared immunopathogenic pathways may enable the selection of targeted therapies that simultaneously control multiple autoimmune conditions, thereby improving disease control and reducing the treatment burden.

items.title: Differences in the clinical profile between isolated lupus anticoagulant and triplepositive antiphospholipid antibody profiles in primary antiphospholipid syndrome.
items.abstract: To compare the clinical phenotype of patients with primary antiphospholipid syndrome who have isolated lupus anticoagulant positivity versus those with triple positivity. This cross-sectional study included two cohorts from two tertiary centers in Brazil comprising patients diagnosed with primary antiphospholipid syndrome. Of 313 patients, 135 were selected and divided into two groups. A total of 99 had isolated lupus anticoagulant positivity and 36 had triple positivity. Most participants were female (58.5%) and White (61.5%), with a mean age of 50.1±12.0 years and a median disease duration of 16 (12-22) years. Both groups showed similar rates of thrombosis (93.9% in the lupus anticoagulant group versus 100% in the triple positivity group, p=0.131) and obstetric events (55.8% versus 60.0%, p=0.754). Microthrombotic and non-thrombotic event rates were also comparable. Hydroxychloroquine use was higher in the triple-positive group (36.1%) than in the lupus anticoagulant group (15.2%, p=0.008). No more severe phenotype was observed in patients with triple positivity compared with those with isolated lupus anticoagulant positivity. The mixed ancestry and demographic composition of the Brazilian population may explain differences compared with more homogeneous populations.

items.title: A critical appraisal of guidelines and recommendations for the management of ANCA-associated vasculitis.
items.abstract: We aimed to appraise 11 currently available guidelines for ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV), identify potential gaps, and provide recommendations for improvement. The guidelines were appraised using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation II (AGREE II) instrument consisting of 23 appraisal criteria/items across six domains (D). Four reviewers independently appraised guidelines and scaled domain scores were calculated. The average score of all guidelines was 4.5 ± 0.8 out of 7.0. Agreement between the reviewers was excellent. British Society for Rheumatology 2025 guidelines scored highest (5.8/7.0), being the only guideline unanimously recommended for use. In 'D1/Scope and purpose', all guidelines achieved high scores. In 'D2/Stakeholder involvement', major gaps were identified in the inclusion of the views and preferences of the target population (2c), with few guidelines including patient representatives, addressing patient participation, or considering patient views. In 'D3/Rigour of development', all but two guidelines received high scores. Implementation of the procedure for updating the guidelines (3 h) and for external review (3 g) was addressed poorly. In 'D4/Clarity of presentation', all guidelines except one received a high score. 'D5/Applicability' had the lowest scores due to gaps in the criteria for monitoring/auditing guideline implementation (5d), resource/cost implications (5c), lack of advice/tools for implementation (5a), and inadequate addressing of facilitators/barriers in guideline application (5a). 'D6/Editorial independence' was addressed well. Several aspects of AAV guidelines could be improved, including the inclusion of patient views and preferences, the processes for translating guidelines into clinical practice, and clearer criteria for monitoring guideline implementation and uptake.

items.title: Case Report: Upfront sotatercept-based triple therapy in high-risk systemic sclerosis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (SSc-PAH) carries a poor prognosis, and treatment decisions are often complicated by coexisting left-heart disease, lung disease, chronic thromboembolic disease, or pulmonary veno-occlusive disease-like vasculopathy. The role of sotatercept as part of initial therapy in treatment-naive SSc-PAH has not been established. We report a 60-year-old man with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis, first recognized at referral 3 years after the onset of skin symptoms, and high-risk precapillary PAH. Careful evaluation showed no clinically significant parenchymal lung disease, chronic thromboembolic disease, or post-capillary physiology. Upfront therapy was started with macitentan, tadalafil, and sotatercept, with short-term dobutamine support for low-output hemodynamics. After 3 months, right heart catheterization showed marked improvement: pulmonary vascular resistance decreased from 12.6 to 3.7 Wood units, mean pulmonary arterial pressure decreased from 43 to 30 mmHg, and cardiac index increased from 1.50 to 2.90 L/min/m². World Health Organization functional class improved from III to II, and risk status shifted to low risk by REVEAL Lite 2, COMPERA 2.0, and the Japanese Circulation Society/Japanese Pulmonary Circulation and Pulmonary Hypertension Society 2025 model. No sotatercept-related adverse events were observed. This case documents the short-term course of upfront sotatercept-based triple therapy in carefully selected high-risk precapillary SSc-PAH.

items.title: Intestinal Behçet's Disease in the Era of Biologics: Current Evidence and Future Perspectives.
items.abstract: Intestinal Behçet's disease (BD) is a rare but potentially life-threatening manifestation of Behçet's syndrome characterized by recurrent gastrointestinal symptoms and typical intestinal ulceration on endoscopic and radiological examinations. Despite advances in understanding intestinal BD, its diagnosis and management remain challenging because of heterogeneous clinical presentations, the absence of validated diagnostic biomarkers, and limited high-quality evidence to guide the optimal use and sequencing of biologic therapies. This review summarizes recent advances in the pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment of intestinal BD, with particular emphasis on emerging therapeutic strategies, precision medicine, and future research priorities aimed at optimizing long-term clinical outcomes.

items.title: A mixture of pomegranate peels and propolis extracts reduces inflammation associated with rheumatoid arthritis in vivo .
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic condition characterized by the infiltration of immune and inflammatory cells into the synovial membranes, which often leads to severe damage to cartilage and bone. In spite of their efficacy, drug-based therapies produce severe side effects. Therefore, there remains an unmet need for non-pharmacological treatments with a low toxicity profile and limited costs. Propolis has been used since ancient times for the treatment of wounds, ulcers, infections, eczemas, myalgia, and rheumatism. Similarly, the traditional use of all parts of pomegranate ( Punica granatum L.) is documented across Egyptian, Persian, and Chinese cultures for the treatment of infections and inflammations. This study aimed at the development of preparations containing bioactive compounds derived from propolis and pomegranate peels, inspired by traditional recipes used in rural areas of southern Italy, to validate their efficacy in counteracting the inflammation associated with RA. A preliminary screening led to the selection of the most promising preparation, composed by propolis and pomegranate peel extracts in a ratio 1:2 (Pp1:2). It underwent a complete chemical characterization by both qualitative and quantitative LC-MS analyses and was tested on a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mouse model. In vitro tests showed that Pp1:2 treatment of M1 stimulated by LPS/IFNγ reduces cell polarization; furthermore, it reverts the pro-inflammatory effects induced by IL-1β on synoviocytes. In vivo experiments, conducted by administering Pp1:2 orally to a suitable murine model, confirmed the ability of the preparation to reduce sensibly RA-like inflammatory effects, as inferred by the change observed in mice paws volume and other RA-related parameters. Furthermore, histological analyses revealed a reduction in the number of M1 macrophages in mice paws following Pp1:2 treatment, and an attenuation of the pathological remodeling of collagen IV and of ICAM-1 expression, compared to untreated controls.

items.title: Case Report and literature review: complications of the association between rheumatoid arthritis and tuberculosis.
items.abstract: Pulmonary tuberculosis is one of the major public health issues globally. According to the World Health Organization, it is among the top 10 causes of death caused by a single pathogen. In Romania, its reported incidence rate in 2024 was approximately 60 per 100,000 people, making it the country with the highest incidence in Europe. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease characterized by the destruction of the small joints along with symmetrical distribution and multiorgan involvement. Pulmonary manifestations are more common in males with positive serology and can involve the lungs, airways, or pleura. Short-term corticotherapy may be initiated in patients with severe symptoms, and biological therapy (anti-TNF alpha drugs) may be used in those with inefficiency of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, with an increased risk for disseminated forms of tuberculosis in those with latent infection. We present the case of a 38-year-old male patient with a 5-year history of seropositive RA who was treated with methotrexate and methylprednisolone, without any prior investigations for latent tuberculosis infection or any chest radiography performed, and was admitted with severe respiratory failure. The results of thoracic computed tomography showed bilateral pneumothorax and pneumomediastinum, with pulmonary lesions suggestive of a diagnosis of tuberculosis, which was confirmed by bacteriological testing of samples. The coexistence of two severe diseases-one requiring immunosuppressive treatment and the other one favored by immunosuppression-in a country with a high prevalence of tuberculosis infection and in the absence of latent tuberculosis infection screening or periodic pulmonological assessment can lead to severe, life-threatening complications that require complex, multidisciplinary, long-term, and expensive management.

items.title: Case Report: Clinical characteristics and management strategies of intraspinal tophaceous gout: a case series and literature review.
items.abstract: Intraspinal tophaceous gout, defined as monosodium urate crystal deposition within the effective spinal canal causing neural compression, is a rare subtype of spinal gout with no unified diagnostic standard. Despite documented gout history, it is frequently misdiagnosed preoperatively. We retrospectively analyzed five male patients with pathologically confirmed intraspinal tophaceous gout (median age 25 years, range 21-48) admitted to two tertiary hospitals between January 2018 and May 2026, alongside a systematic literature review of strictly defined cases. The preoperative misdiagnosis rate was 60%. Computed tomography values of 142-272 Hounsfield units provided diagnostic clues, yet no patient underwent preoperative dual-energy computed tomography. Three patients underwent open decompression with fusion, one endoscopic decompression, and one computed tomography-guided biopsy followed by conservative observation; pathology confirmed gouty tophus or granuloma in all. One patient developed a postoperative intraspinal hematoma on day 4, a previously unreported complication. Long-term follow-up revealed multiple vertebral compression fractures and thoracic spinal cord injury in one patient with poor compliance with urate-lowering therapy, a bone event that requires long-term vigilance. Pooled analysis of the 38 strictly defined cases (33 literature cases plus this series) confirmed that the preoperative misdiagnosis rate exceeds 50% and that most lesions are epidural. Intraspinal tophaceous gout should be considered in young male patients with back pain and neural deficits, even with known gout history. A stepwise imaging strategy, individualized surgical or biopsy-first management, vigilant postoperative monitoring, and long-term urate-lowering therapy are essential for optimal outcomes.

items.title: Matrix Metalloproteinase-9-Activated Dually-Quenched Fluorescence Nanoprobe for Sensitive Imaging of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Fluorescence probes that enable sensitive and real-time in vivo imaging of matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) hold high promise for early clinical diagnosis of intractable rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but they remain scarcely developed. Herein, we developed the dually quenched fluorescence nanoprobe P-IR780-NP for sensitive in vivo imaging of RA. To prepare P-IR780-NP, a molecular precursor Cys(StBu)-Pro-Leu-Gly-Leu-Lys(IR780)-CBT (P-IR780) was synthesized. Under reductive conditions, P-IR780 undergoes a 2-cyanobenzothiazole-cysteine (CBT-Cys) click reaction to form a cyclic dimer (P-IR780-Dimer), which subsequently assembles into P-IR780-NP nanoparticles. The sequential cyclization and assembly processes cause intramolecular and intermolecular quenching of the conjugated IR780 fluorophore, respectively, thereby collectively minimizing background fluorescence. In vitro studies confirmed that MMP-9 specifically cleaved P-IR780-Dimer, triggering nanoparticle disassembly and consequent 8.6-fold fluorescence enhancement. In MMP-9-overexpressing macrophages, P-IR780-NP produced 1.8-fold stronger fluorescence signals compared to the MMP-9-inhibited control group. Notably, in vivo imaging of RA mice revealed a 3.7-fold higher fluorescence intensity in affected joints relative to healthy controls, demonstrating the enhanced sensitivity of P-IR780-NP for in vivo RA imaging. We anticipate that P-IR780-NP could be applied for early clinical diagnosis of RA in the near future.

items.title: GZMK⁺CD8⁺ T Cells Induce Acinar Cell Senescence and Salivary Secretion Impairment in Sjögren's Syndrome via Mitochondrial Dysfunction and TMEM16A Chloride Channel Disruption.
items.abstract: Immune cell-mediated damage to acinar cells plays a central role in Sjögren's syndrome (SS) pathogenesis, with T-cell recruitment being critical in the early stages. In this study, single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to generate transcriptomic profiles of labial gland tissues from SS patients, focusing on GZMK⁺CD8⁺ T cells and their correlation with SS clinical pathology. The role of GZMK⁺CD8⁺ T cells in inducing acinar cell senescence and secretory dysfunction was investigated by co-culturing SMG-C6 acinar cells with GZMK⁺CD8⁺ T cells and recombinant granzyme K. Mechanistically, GZMK induces oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, thereby promoting senescent phenotypes in acinar cells. Additionally, GZMK-mediated downregulation of TMEM16A contributes to reduced chloride transport and salivary secretion dysfunction. This study provides novel insights into the immune-epithelial crosstalk in SS progression by revealing the relationship between GZMK⁺CD8⁺ T cells and acinar cells. This pathogenic immune-epithelial interaction may offer a promising therapeutic strategy to mitigate SS progression in the early stages and restore salivary secretion in SS patients.

items.title: Multifunctional Methotrexate-Laden Nanotherapy Modulates the Joint-Brain Axis and Attenuates Associated Neuroinflammation in an Experimental Model of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease marked by persistent synovial inflammation, cartilage erosion, and systemic manifestations, including cognitive and neuropsychiatric complications. Increasing evidence highlights the bidirectional interplay of the joint-brain axis between peripheral inflammation and central nervous system dysfunction as a critical contributor to RA pathogenesis. Current frontline treatments, such as methotrexate (M), face challenges, including poor bioavailability, off-target toxicity, and limited efficacy in addressing neuroinflammation. To address these limitations, we developed methotrexate-loaded tryptophan-Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)-glutathione nanomicelles (M-WPG NMs), an advanced enzyme- and pH-responsive drug delivery platform designed for targeted release at inflamed joints. In collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) models, M-WPG NMs demonstrated superior therapeutic efficacy by significantly reducing joint inflammation, downregulating pro-inflammatory cytokines, and preserving joint architecture. Additionally, M-WPG NMs attenuated microglial activation and mitigated associated neuroinflammation in chronic RA, offering dual modulation of both peripheral and central inflammatory responses. This multifunctional nanocarrier improves methotrexate delivery, enhances therapeutic outcomes, and addresses the often-overlooked neurological components of RA. Our findings support the application of M-WPG NMs as a next-generation nanomedicine for comprehensive RA management, capable of controlling disease progression while offering protection against RA-induced cognitive dysfunction.

items.title: A nanoengineered MSC therapeutic for synergistic therapy of lupus nephritis via cfDNA clearance and targeted immunomodulation.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) remains a clinical challenge due to the dose-limiting toxicity of conventional immunosuppressants and the poor engraftment/efficacy of mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapies. We report a novel nanoengineered MSC therapeutic for LN by engineering MSCs with a cell-free DNA (cfDNA)-targeting dendritic nanogel. To obtain the hybrid MSC-G3K@T system, we coupled tacrolimus-loaded, disulfide-crosslinked polylysine dendrimer nanogels (G3K@T) onto the MSC membrane. Our system exploits two synergistic targeting strategies: the innate homing capacity of MSCs, plus the specific affinity of the cationic G3K dendrimer for anionic cfDNA, which enriches in inflamed kidneys. Our system acts through two coordinated actions: the nanogel responds to the oxidative renal microenvironment and releases tacrolimus in a spatiotemporally controlled manner, thereby suppressing T-cell activation. At the same time, it scavenges cfDNA, blocking TLR-mediated pro-inflammatory signaling. Working together with the inherent immunomodulatory functions of MSCs, this dual-action strategy yielded robust efficacy in MRL/lpr mice, including a significant reversal of T-cell dysregulation, restoration of glomerular integrity, and reduction of proteinuria and IgG deposition. We propose that MSC-G3K@T offers a promising route to augment cell-based therapies, creating a versatile platform that could be used to treat autoimmune and inflammatory diseases.

items.title: Risk of myocardial infarction in adults with gout treated with allopurinol: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: AimsAlthough allopurinol is used for urate-lowering therapy, its effect on myocardial infarction risk remains unclear. This study assessed the association between allopurinol use and myocardial infarction in adults with gout.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PROSPERO registration (CRD420261305257). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to January 2026. Observational studies of adults with confirmed gout that reported adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for myocardial infarction and separately identifiable allopurinol exposure were included. Pooled estimates were calculated using an inverse-variance random-effects model with the Paule-Mandel estimator. Robustness was assessed through leave-one-out, active-comparator, and Hartung-Knapp sensitivity analyses.ResultsFour retrospective cohort studies met the revised eligibility criteria. In the primary random-effects analysis, allopurinol use was associated with a lower risk of myocardial infarction (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.76-0.94; I 2 = 0%). However, the association was not statistically significant after excluding the study contributing the greatest weight (HR 1.04; 95% CI 0.79-1.36), when restricted to active comparators (HR 1.04; 95% CI 0.79-1.36), or using the Hartung-Knapp adjustment (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.71-1.00).ConclusionAllopurinol therapy was associated with a modest but significant reduction in myocardial infarction risk in adults with gout.

items.title: METTL14 Declines Th17/Treg Ratio Via the m6A Modification of DUSP23 to Alleviate Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: The imbalance between T helper (Th) 17 cells and regulatory T (Treg) cells is involved in the progression of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Dual-specificity protein phosphatase 23 (DUSP23) expression is elevated in CD4 + T cells from SLE patients, though its function role remains unclear. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), serum, and CD4 + T cells were isolated from blood samples of SLE patients. MRL/lpr mice were used to investigate the role of METTL14 in vivo. The expression of methyltransferase-like 14 (METTL14) and DUSP23 in cells was determined by RT-qPCR or immunoblotting. The proportions of Th17 and Treg cells were primarily determined by flow cytometry. The expression of key transcription factors and the secretion of related cytokines were evaluated by immunoblotting or ELISA. MeRIP was performed to assess the m6A modification of DUSP23 mRNA. DUSP23 is elevated in PBMCs from SLE patients. Inhibition of DUSP23 reduced Th17 but increased Treg cells proportions within CD4 + T cells in vitro. A negative correlation was observed between DUSP23 and METTL14 expression in SLE-derived PBMCs. Mechanistically, METTL14 enhanced the m6A modification of DUSP23 mRNA, thereby promoting its decay. In MRL/lpr mice, METTL14 overexpression reduced Th17/Treg imbalance and ameliorated renal injury. The results demonstrate that METTL14 ameliorates murine SLE by attenuating the Th17/Treg imbalance through m6A-mediated decay of DUSP23, providing novel insights for SLE diagnosis and therapy.

items.title: Longitudinal clinical and musculoskeletal ultrasound assessment after switching from oral to subcutaneous methotrexate in rheumatoid arthritis: a two-center real-world study.
items.abstract: Subcutaneous methotrexate (SC MTX) provides more reliable bioavailability than oral MTX; however, longitudinal real-world data incorporating musculoskeletal ultrasound (MSUS) remain limited. We aimed to evaluate longitudinal changes in clinical disease activity and ultrasound-detected synovitis, particularly power Doppler (PD) activity, after switching from oral to SC MTX in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This two-center retrospective cohort study included 57 patients with RA who switched from oral to SC MTX in routine clinical practice. Clinical disease activity measures (DAS28-CRP, SDAI, and CDAI) were assessed at baseline and at 1, 3, and 6 months. In patients with available longitudinal MSUS follow-up, semiquantitative gray-scale (GS) and PD scores of the representative joint were evaluated at the same time points. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with Dunnett-adjusted comparisons versus baseline. Baseline characteristics of patients with and without 6-month ultrasound follow-up were compared using standardized mean differences. Clinical disease activity improved over time following the switch to SC MTX. Significant reductions from baseline were observed for SDAI, CDAI, and DAS28-CRP at all follow-up visits. Representative-joint PD scores showed a significant overall longitudinal reduction, with adjusted mean decreases of 0.64 points at 1 month and 0.95 points at 3 months compared with baseline. Although representative-joint PD scores also showed a numerical reduction at 6 months, statistical significance was not maintained after adjustment for multiple comparisons. In contrast, representative-joint GS scores showed numerical improvement but no statistically significant overall longitudinal change. DAS28-CRP remission (<2.6) was achieved in 30/56 (53.6%) patients at 1 month, 38/55 (69.1%) at 3 months, and 34/52 (65.4%) at 6 months. MSUS follow-up was available in 40 patients at baseline, 29 at 1 month, 20 at 3 months, and 17 at 6 months. Most missing 6-month ultrasound assessments were attributable to clinical remission or low disease activity. In this real-world observational study, switching from oral to SC MTX was associated with early reductions in representative-joint PD-detected synovitis, with statistically significant improvement observed at 1 and 3 months, together with improvements in clinical disease activity over six months. Because of the retrospective design, absence of a comparator group, and incomplete ultrasound follow-up, residual confounding and selection bias cannot be excluded. These findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating but suggest that MSUS, particularly PD assessment, may provide a useful objective tool for monitoring inflammatory activity after switching to SC MTX in routine clinical practice. Not applicable.

items.title: Probability of audiovestibular pathologies, hearing loss and cochlear function in patients with ankylosing spondylitis in a tertiary institute.
items.abstract: To describe the auditory function in a sample of patients with ankylosing spondylitis and to determine the conditional probability of occurrence among variables related to auditory characteristics through joint probability analysis. This was a cross-sectional and descriptive study. Sociodemographic and auditory characteristics were collected from 49 patients. Descriptive analysis and probabilistic intersection analysis were conducted to determine the joint probability between variables. Superficial hearing loss was observed in 22.4%, a decline in high frequencies in 20.4%, a sensorineural hearing loss pattern in 47% of right ears and 49% of left ears, As-type tympanograms in 49% of right ears and 57.1% of left ears, and absence of ipsilateral stapedius reflexes (predominantly in the left ear) in 55.1%. Transient otoacoustic emissions exhibited inadequate reproducibility, particularly 4000 and 1000 Hz, in both ears, with tinnitus being the most common audiovestibular symptom (36.7%). The joint probability that a patient is male, has ankylosing spondylitis with 10 years of disease progression, and presents a sensorineural hearing loss pattern in either the right or left ear, is 27.7%. Sensorineural hearing loss is highly prevalent among patients with ankylosing spondylitis. The duration of the disease is a significant factor influencing the presentation of hearing loss and audiovestibular symptoms. items.title: A Mitochondria-Modulating Nanosystem for Rheumatoid Arthritis Immunotherapy via Inflammatory Cascade Disruption.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic autoimmune disease characterized by chronic inflammation within joints, where macrophage-driven inflammatory cascade caused by mitochondrial dysfunction significantly contributes to the pathogenesis. Through recruitment and activation of neutrophils from circulation, these macrophages promote the release of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), leading to synovitis exacerbation and tissue damage. To disrupt this closely linked cycle, we present a mitochondria-modulating nanosystem (NM@APDAase) targeting the inflammatory cascade for RA immunotherapy. The neutrophil membrane-camouflaged nanomaterials are directed to inflamed joints, where the released AP39 effectively restores mitochondrial function by serving as a mild electron donor and uncoupler. This reprograms macrophages from a pro-inflammatory to an anti-inflammatory phenotype, thereby eliminating the primary source of inflammation. Notably, the co-loaded DNase I and polydopamine scaffold work synergistically to clear pre-existing NETs and scavenge ROS. In vivo studies demonstrate that NM@APDAase significantly alleviates RA pathology as evidenced by reduced inflammatory responses, mitigated cartilage erosion and reduced bone destruction. Our work highlights the promise of mitochondria-modulating nanomaterials for treating RA through directed disruption of the inflammatory cascade.

items.title: Ex vivo JAK and TNF inhibitor-modulated immune signatures guide first-line therapy selection in rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disease for which selecting the most appropriate first targeted therapy remains challenging. We integrated ex vivo immune-cell functional assays, targeted proteomics, clinical outcomes, and a three-dimensional (3D) synovial model to identify treatment-associated molecular signatures and evaluate their relationship with subsequent response to Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) or tumour necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi). Peripheral blood mononuclear cells and neutrophils from 48 b/tsDMARDs-naïve RA patients were cultured with autologous serum and treated ex vivo with Baricitinib or Etanercept to assess proliferation, adhesion, NETosis, and 92 inflammation-related proteins. The resulting JAKi- and TNFi-modulated protein signatures were subsequently evaluated in pretreatment serum from four independent RA treatment cohorts (n = 223; naïve and non-naïve). Unsupervised clustering was used to identify molecular subgroups, which were related to longitudinal DAS28-CRP outcomes at 3, 6, and 12 months. Logistic regression, neural network, and random forest models were evaluated using repeated nested cross-validation in naïve patients to discriminate treatment-specific 6-month remission outcomes. In a subset of naïve remission achievers, paired baseline and 6-month sera were applied to a 3D synovial micromass model. Ex vivo JAKi and TNFi comparably modulated immune cell functions but induced distinct protein signatures with limited overlap. When evaluated in pretreatment baseline serum, these signatures stratified b/tsDMARD-naïve patients into clusters with different baseline inflammatory profiles and treatment-specific ΔDAS28-CRP. High baseline expression of a drug-specific signature was associated with remission with the corresponding therapy and failure to achieve remission with the alternative treatment. Under repeated nested cross-validation, logistic regression showed the highest mean discrimination among the models, with an AUC of 0.70 (SD, 0.03; empirical 2.5th-97.5th percentile, 0.65-0.75) for distinguishing treatment-specific remission outcomes in b/tsDMARD-naïve RA. In remission achievers, 6-month sera from either therapy significantly reduced synovial lining thickness in 3D micromasses versus baseline. Ex vivo-derived JAKi- and TNFi-associated immune-related protein signatures, integrated within a machine-learning framework, showed moderate discriminatory ability for treatment-specific remission patterns in b/tsDMARD-naïve RA and, together with complementary evidence of reduced synovial lining thickness in remission achievers, support further investigation of biomarker-informed selection between JAKi and TNFi as first targeted therapies.

items.title: Ianalumab for the Treatment of Patients with Sjögren's Disease.
items.abstract: Sjögren's disease is a complex, systemic autoimmune disease with no approved targeted therapies. Ianalumab is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody with a dual mechanism of action, depleting B cells through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and inhibiting B-cell activation and survival through blockade of B-cell activating factor receptor. We conducted two 52-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease. Patients in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ianalumab (300 mg monthly) or placebo; patients in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 300 mg of ianalumab monthly or every 3 months or placebo. The primary end point was the change from baseline in the score on the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) at week 48 (scores range from 0 to 123, with higher scores indicating greater disease activity). The first key secondary end point in the hierarchical plan for the NEPTUNUS-1 trial was an ESSDAI response (≥5-point reduction) at week 48; for the NEPTUNUS-2 trial, it was the change from baseline in the score on the Sjögren's Syndrome Symptom Diary (SSSD) or EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index (ESSPRI) at week 48. Overall, 275 patients underwent randomization in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial (ianalumab monthly, 137 patients; placebo, 138 patients) and 504 in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial (ianalumab monthly, 168 patients; ianalumab every 3 months, 167 patients; and placebo, 169 patients). In both trials, ianalumab monthly led to a significantly greater decrease in the ESSDAI score at week 48 than placebo, with a between-group difference of -1.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI], -2.6 to 0.0; P = 0.0496) in NEPTUNUS-1 and -1.0 points (95% CI, -2.0 to 0.0; P = 0.04) in NEPTUNUS-2. No significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI scores were observed at week 48. The incidence of serious adverse events was similar with ianalumab and placebo. Nonserious local injection-site and systemic injection-related reactions were more common in the ianalumab groups. In these two trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease, ianalumab at a dose of 300 mg monthly resulted in a significantly greater decrease in disease activity at week 48 than placebo, although there were no significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI symptom scores. (Funded by Novartis Pharma; NEPTUNUS-1 and NEPTUNUS-2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05350072 and NCT05349214, respectively.).

items.title: Letter regarding "Serum gelsolin as a biomarker for differentiating familial Mediterranean fever from juvenile idiopathic arthritis in children".
items.abstract: Dişçi et al. reported promising discrimination between familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) and juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) using serum gelsolin (Gsn), achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.82. However, the performance observed in small, selected groups of children with established diagnoses may not generalize to patients presenting with diagnostic uncertainty. Deriving and evaluating the diagnostic threshold within the same cohort, without independent validation, may lead to overly optimistic estimates of sensitivity and specificity. Furthermore, the incremental diagnostic value of Gsn beyond standard clinical assessment and routine laboratory markers remains unclear. To determine if Gsn offers clinically useful information for differentiating FMF from JIA, prospective studies are needed. These studies should enroll consecutive children with diagnostic uncertainty, utilize prespecified thresholds, and include independent validation.

items.title: Imaging-guided treatment strategy compared to standard care in at-risk individuals for rheumatoid arthritis: a cost-utility analysis.
items.abstract: Some individuals present with symptoms before rheumatoid arthritis (RA) develops, and trials suggest that early treatment during this at-risk phase may be effective. This study evaluated the cost-utility of three imaging strategies—conventional MRI, modified Dixon MRI and ultrasound—combined with early treatment compared with watchful waiting in individuals at risk of RA, stratified by autoantibody status. A decision tree combined with a Markov model was developed to estimate costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) over a 2-year time horizon. Model inputs were derived from the TREAT EARLIER trial for treated patients at risk of developing RA, clinically suspect arthralgia (CSA) cohorts for untreated at-risk patients and the early arthritis clinic for patients with undifferentiated arthritis or RA. Cost-utility analyses were conducted from both the societal- and healthcare perspectives. Probabilistic and deterministic sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess the uncertainty of the results, and several scenarios were explored. Dutch hospital setting. Individuals at risk of developing RA, stratified by autoantibody status. Watchful waiting was compared with three imaging strategies—conventional MRI, modified Dixon MRI and ultrasound—combined with early treatment (single intramuscular glucocorticoid injection and 1-year methotrexate course) in patients with positive subclinical inflammation. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) of the interventions compared with watchful waiting. Cost-effectiveness probabilities were estimated at a willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold of €50,000 per QALY. From a societal perspective, autoantibody-positive patients showed cost savings of €1,183 (-5348 to 2861) (ultrasound) to €1,825 (-8041 to 3861) (modified Dixon MRI). Autoantibody-negative patients had incremental costs from €21 (-3843 to 3856) (conventional MRI) to -€409 (-4499 to 3681) (modified Dixon MRI). QALYs gained ranged from 0.006 (-0.04 to 0.06) to 0.016 (-0.08 to 0.11). Probability of cost-effectiveness was 75%–80% for autoantibody-positive patients and 56%–70% for autoantibody-negative patients at a WTP of €50 000/QALY. Results were less pronounced from a healthcare perspective. Deterministic sensitivity analysis showed the results were robust to most changes in parameters; however, the results were sensitive to extreme changes in parameters related to treatment effects on quality of life (QoL) and productivity and disutilities due to treatment-related side effects. Imaging-guided early treatment for arthralgia at-risk for RA may be cost-effective, particularly for autoantibody-positive patients, irrespective of imaging modality. Modified Dixon MRI seems most promising and requires further validation in CSA. TREAT EARLIER trial: EudraCT, 2014–004472-35 and the Netherlands Trial Register, NTR4853-trial-NL4599.

items.title: Bidirectional regulation of the PD-1 pathway: Tumor immune exhaustion versus lupus nephritis T cells activation.
items.abstract: The PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint pathway serves as a core regulatory hub that maintains peripheral immune tolerance. In different disease contexts, this axis exhibits opposing outcomes. In cancer, sustained antigenic stimulation elevates PD-1 expression and locks T cells into an exhaustion phenotype-a state characterized by progressive loss of effector functions, coordinated upregulation of multiple inhibitory receptors, and a TOX-driven epigenetic landscape. Conversely, in lupus nephritis (LN)-a severe autoimmune complication of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)-PD-1 + T cells (both CD8 + and CD4 + subsets) undergo clonal expansion, display a highly activated phenotype, and produce abundant granzyme B, perforin, and IFN-γ, thereby directly inflicting renal tissue damage. Importantly, LN-associated PD-1 + T cells are not uniformly exhausted; single-cell studies suggest that activated and partially exhausted subsets can co-exist. This review systematically elucidates the molecular, cellular, and microenvironmental bases that determine the bidirectional nature of PD-1 signaling-driving T cells toward exhaustion in cancer while promoting T cell activation in LN. Key differentiating factors underlying this divergence include the intensity and persistence of antigen stimulation, activation of the TOX-dependent exhaustion epigenetic program, the cytokine milieu composition (type I interferons, IL-12, IL-6), the balance between co-stimulatory and co-inhibitory signals, and the strikingly different metabolic environments-a nutrient-deprived, hypoxic tumor microenvironment versus an inflamed, metabolically active kidney in LN. As a theoretical synthesis, we propose a conceptual "balancing window" model of PD-1 signal strength to describe this bidirectional regulatory mechanism; this model is hypothesis-generating and not clinically validated. Finally, we discuss the clinical translation implications of this framework, encompassing PD-1 agonistic strategies in autoimmune diseases (still largely preclinical/early clinical), PD-1 blockade in cancer therapy, and the iatrogenic lupus-like syndrome induced by immune checkpoint inhibitors-the latter providing biological plausibility rather than definitive proof of causality. All proposed biomarkers and algorithms are presented as investigational tools not yet ready for routine clinical practice. Moreover, LN pathogenesis involves multiple pathways beyond T cells-including immune complexes, complement, B cells, and innate immunity-and the PD-1 axis should be considered within this broader context.

items.title: Routine antinuclear antibody testing as an independent prognostic biomarker for end-stage renal disease in ANCA-associated vasculitis: a longitudinal cohort study.
items.abstract: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV) frequently involves the kidney. Although a subset of AAV patients tests positive for serum antinuclear antibody (ANA), data on the association between ANA positivity and progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD) in AAV remain limited. This retrospective cohort study enrolled 236 patients with AAV. Patients were categorized according to ANA status. Baseline clinical, laboratory, and renal histopathological parameters were analyzed. The primary endpoint was progression to ESRD, assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses. Risk stratification was performed based on ANA status and baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Serum ANA positivity was observed in 37.3% of patients. Patients with positive ANA had worse baseline renal function and more prominent IgG deposition on renal pathology. The cumulative incidence of ESRD was significantly higher in the ANA-positive group during follow-up. Multivariable Cox regression confirmed ANA positivity as an independent risk factor for ESRD after adjusting for baseline eGFR and age. Risk stratification combining ANA status and eGFR (<30 mL/min/1.73m 2 ) identified a high-risk subgroup with a 7.19-fold increased ESRD risk. In sensitivity analyses, ANA positivity remained significantly associated with ESRD after additional adjustment for proteinuria, disease activity, ANCA specificity, or treatment. Routine serum ANA testing provides valuable prognostic information for predicting progression to ESRD in AAV patients. The combination of ANA positivity and reduced eGFR offers a simple and clinically actionable risk stratification model. These findings support the integration of ANA status into routine clinical risk assessment for AAV, providing a simple and actionable tool for the early identification of high-risk patients requiring intensified monitoring.

items.title: Therapeutic potential of zinc supplementation in rheumatoid arthritis: clinical evidence, molecular mechanisms, and formulation-specific effects.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disorder primarily affecting the synovial joints, characterized by persistent synovitis, progressive joint destruction, and systemic complications that contribute to significant morbidity. Despite advances in disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs and biologic therapies, many patients fail to achieve sustained disease control or experience treatment-related adverse effects, highlighting the need for safe adjunctive strategies. Zinc, an essential trace element with critical roles in immune regulation, antioxidant defense, and inflammatory signaling, has gained increasing attention in the pathogenesis and management of RA. Clinical studies consistently report altered zinc homeostasis and reduced circulating zinc levels in RA, which are associated with increased disease activity, oxidative stress, and immune dysregulation. However, human interventional studies evaluating zinc supplementation remain limited, involve relatively small sample sizes, and report heterogeneous findings. In contrast, experimental studies in validated animal models have more consistently demonstrated anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects of zinc, including modulation of macrophage and T-cell activation, cytokine production, synovial fibroblast behaviour, and bone remodelling. Importantly, the therapeutic effects of zinc appear to be formulation-dependent, as organic zinc salts, chelated forms, and emerging nano-based formulations have demonstrated superior bioavailability and anti-inflammatory efficacy compared with conventional inorganic salts. This review aims to explain the molecular and immunological mechanisms underlying the effect of zinc in RA, evaluates findings from clinical and preclinical studies of zinc supplementation, and highlights formulation-specific considerations relevant to clinical practice. While existing evidence supports the potential of zinc as a safe and beneficial adjunct to conventional RA therapy, further well-designed randomized clinical trials are required to establish optimal dosing strategies and identify patient populations most likely to benefit.

items.title: Therapeutic modulation of inflammation and oxidative stress in rheumatoid arthritis through Choerospondias axillaris intervention: evidence from in-vitro and in-vivo studies.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disorder, and current therapeutic approaches often present adverse effects on human health. This highlights the need to explore dietary sources of bioactive compounds for RA management. This study aimed to evaluate the potential of a Choerospondias axillaris (C. axillaris) chewable nutraceutical tablet (LT), formulated from the underutilized fruit of C. axillaris, for RA management. LTs were prepared by direct compression using C. axillaris fruit powder as the principal ingredient. The tablets were characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). Antioxidant activity was evaluated using the DPPH free-radical scavenging assay. Potential RA-associated targets of C. axillaris were predicted using PharmMapper, followed by Cytoscape-based network analysis and Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analyses. Selected targets were evaluated in synovial fibroblasts using quantitative PCR (qPCR) and in a collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rat model. Molecular docking was performed to assess interactions between major bioactive compounds and selected RA-related proteins. The formulated tablets contained detectable mineral elements and phytochemical constituents. Network pharmacology identified 20 potential targets associated with C. axillaris activity against RA. Molecular docking revealed potential interactions between selected bioactive compounds and key RA-related proteins. In vitro treatment reduced MAPK14, MMP9, and IL2 expression in synovial fibroblasts. In vivo treatment also suppressed inflammatory responses in the plasma of CIA rats. These findings indicate that C. axillaris bioactive compounds may modulate molecular targets associated with RA-related inflammation. The findings support further investigation of C. axillaris-derived nutraceutical formulations for RA management.

items.title: Peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer and choroidal vascularity correlate with disease activity in systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) confers risk of subclinical neurovascular injury. We assessed retinal and choroidal structural alterations using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) and evaluated their relationship with disease activity and immunological markers. In this prospective, cross-sectional study, 70 SLE patients and 35 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent comprehensive ophthalmic examination. SD-OCT with enhanced depth imaging was used to assess peripapillary retinal nerve fibre layer (pRNFL) thickness, macular thickness, and choroidal vascularity index (CVI). Disease activity was measured using the SLE Disease Activity Index-2 K (SLEDAI-2 K). Patients were stratified into active (SLEDAI ≥ 6, n = 18) and inactive (SLEDAI ≤ 5, n = 52) subgroups. Compared to controls, SLE patients had significantly thinner global pRNFL (94.5 ± 5.0 μm vs. 100.5 ± 5.0 μm, p < 0.001) and lower CVI (65.6 ± 2.0% vs. 68.9 ± 2.0%, p < 0.001). Thinning was most pronounced in the temporal superior (TS) and temporal inferior (TI) sectors. Active SLE patients showed greater pRNFL thinning and lower CVI than inactive patients (p < 0.01). SLEDAI scores correlated negatively with temporal pRNFL thickness (TS: r=-0.58; TI: r=-0.56) and CVI (r=-0.63) (all p < 0.001). Anti-dsDNA positivity correlated with reduced pRNFL and CVI, while complement C3 levels showed positive correlations. SD-OCT reveals significant temporal pRNFL thinning and reduced CVI in SLE patients, correlating with systemic disease activity and immunologic markers. These findings support the retina and choroid as accessible sites reflecting SLE-related neurovascular inflammation and contribute to understanding of ocular involvement in disease pathophysiology; longitudinal studies are needed to determine their utility for disease monitoring.

items.title: Underreporting of sacroiliac joint structural abnormalities on routine abdominal CT in axial spondyloarthritis: a longitudinal workflow analysis.
items.abstract: To quantify documentation of predefined, conspicuous sacroiliac joint (SIJ) structural abnormalities on routine abdominal CT in patients with established axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) and identify associated factors. This retrospective longitudinal study evaluated 516 abdominal CT examinations from 188 patients with established SpA. Two readers applied a predefined hierarchical SIJ classification, with adjudication of disagreements. The primary analysis included 226 Moderate or Major examinations; all had fusion-based patterns. Patient-clustered logistic generalized estimating equations included workflow, request-level context, structural severity, prior recognition, and scan year. SIJ findings were absent from 152 of 226 reports (67.3%). Total fusion was unreported in 90 of 136 examinations (66.2%), including 83 of 129 with bilateral total fusion (64.3%). Crude non-reporting was 89.2% in acute care and 50.0% in rheumatology. The four-examination MSK-oriented subgroup was combined with rheumatology for modeling. Adjusted non-reporting was 82.7% in acute care and 50.6% in the combined MSK-pathway, a 32.1-point difference (95% CI, 6.2-52.0); the corresponding OR was 0.20 (95% CI, 0.05-0.75). Structural severity and request-level context were not independently associated with non-reporting. Documentation of conspicuous SIJ structural abnormalities on routine abdominal CT was frequently absent and varied by workflow. Including a field for SIJ findings in structured abdominal CT reports may lead more radiologists to look for joint abnormalities. Automated detection requires external and prospective validation before clinical implementation.

items.title: Prevalence of systemic lupus erythematosus in New Zealand primary care: A retrospective descriptive study.
items.abstract: BackgroundSystemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune condition with a high level of morbidity, mortality and healthcare costs. In New Zealand prevalence of the condition has been increasing over time, although studies to date are based on national administrative datasets or hospital records.ObjectiveWe aimed to estimate the prevalence of SLE based on primary care medical records in New Zealand and to evaluate the differences in age, gender and ethnicity.MethodsPotential SLE cases were identified through electronic primary care records from 1 January 2000 to 20 March 2024. All records were manually reviewed to identify the diagnosis based on 2019 European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology classification criteria. Prevalence was based on definite and probable cases.ResultsSixty-eight SLE cases were identified (55 definite, 6 probable, 7 possible) from a total practice population of 96,348. The crude prevalence of SLE estimated using primary care records was 63.3 per 100,000 people in 2024. The World Health Organization age-standardised prevalence was 52.9 per 100,000 people in 2024. SLE prevalence generally increased with advancing age. Women were five times more likely than men to have SLE (RR 5.36, 95% CI 2.63 - 10.93. Pacific people had the highest age-standardised prevalence of SLE (94.1), followed by Asian (58.7), European/Others (48.3) and Māori (42.9 per 100,000).ConclusionThe use of primary care medical records builds on national studies based primarily on administrative databases. Prevalence of SLE is highest in the elderly (>85 years), females and Pacific people based on primary care data in New Zealand.

items.title: Osteonecrosis in Antiphospholipid Syndrome: An Evidence Map and Diagnostic Attribution Framework for a Noncriteria Manifestation.
items.abstract: Osteonecrosis has been reported in antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) positivity, but because it also follows glucocorticoid exposure, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), alcohol use, trauma, pregnancy, transplantation, and thrombophilia, its status as an APS-related manifestation is uncertain, and clinicians lack a structured way to decide whether it is APS-attributable or coincidental. We conducted a structured narrative review with evidence mapping, searching PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus from inception to May 2026 with citation chasing; eligible reports described osteonecrosis, avascular necrosis, aseptic necrosis, or bone infarction in confirmed APS or documented aPL positivity. Twenty-two publications were charted for design, phenotype, osteonecrosis site, diagnostic modality, competing etiologies, and attribution, and synthesized narratively. Reported frequencies ranged from 3.75% and 4.5% for clinically ascertained disease to 20% for asymptomatic magnetic resonance imaging screen-detected disease in steroid-naïve primary APS-estimates that are not directly comparable. Femoral-head disease predominated, but multifocal, bilateral, and atypical-site lesions were repeatedly described. Attribution was strongest in young patients with persistent high-risk aPL, minimal traditional risk factors, and concurrent thrombotic, obstetric, or microvascular features, yet competing causes, especially glucocorticoids and SLE-frequently coexisted. We propose the APSO framework, stratifying attribution into four tiers (high-confidence, probable, uncertain/mixed, and aPL-positive osteonecrosis without classifiable APS) by APS certainty, aPL risk, osteonecrosis phenotype, and competing-cause burden. Osteonecrosis is a candidate noncriteria skeletal manifestation of APS, but aPL positivity alone is insufficient for causal attribution; prospective validation is required. Résumé L’ostéonécrose a été rapportée dans le syndrome des antiphospholipides (SAPL) et en présence d’anticorps antiphospholipides (aPL), mais comme elle peut également survenir après une exposition aux glucocorticoïdes, dans le lupus érythémateux systémique (LES), en cas de consommation d’alcool, de traumatisme, de grossesse, de transplantation et de thrombophilie, son statut en tant que manifestation liée au SAPL reste incertain, et les cliniciens ne disposent pas d’une méthode structurée pour déterminer si elle est attribuable au SAPL ou fortuite. Nous avons réalisé une revue narrative structurée avec cartographie des données probantes, en interrogeant PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase et Scopus depuis leur création jusqu’en mai 2026, complétée par une recherche des citations; les rapports éligibles décrivaient une ostéonécrose, une nécrose avasculaire, une nécrose aseptique ou un infarctus osseux chez des patients ayant un SAPL confirmé ou une positivité documentée des aPL. Vingt-deux publications ont été recensées selon le plan d’étude, le phénotype, le site de l’ostéonécrose, la modalité diagnostique, les étiologies concurrentes et l’attribution, puis synthétisées de manière narrative. Les fréquences rapportées variaient de 3.75% et 4.5% pour la maladie diagnostiquée cliniquement à 20% pour la maladie asymptomatique détectée par dépistage IRM chez des patients atteints de SAPL primaire n’ayant jamais reçu de corticoïdes; ces estimations ne sont pas directement comparables. L’atteinte de la tête fémorale prédominait, mais des lésions multifocales, bilatérales et de siège atypique ont été décrites à plusieurs reprises. L’attribution était la plus forte chez les patients jeunes présentant des aPL persistants à haut risque, peu de facteurs de risque traditionnels et des manifestations thrombotiques, obstétricales ou microvasculaires concomitantes; cependant, des causes concurrentes, en particulier les glucocorticoïdes et le LES, coexistaient fréquemment. Nous proposons le cadre APSO, qui classe l’attribution en quatre niveaux (forte confiance, probable, incertaine/mixte et ostéonécrose avec aPL positifs sans SAPL classifiable) selon la certitude du SAPL, le risque lié aux aPL, le phénotype de l’ostéonécrose et la charge des causes concurrentes. L’ostéonécrose est une manifestation squelettique candidate hors critères du SAPL, mais la seule positivité des aPL ne suffit pas pour une attribution causale; une validation prospective est nécessaire.

items.title: Generalized edema as the initial manifestation of Anti-TIF1γ-positive dermatomyositis associated with ovarian cancer.
items.abstract: Generalized edema is an uncommon manifestation of dermatomyositis (DM) and may lead clinicians to consider alternative systemic conditions. Anti-transcriptional intermediary factor 1 gamma (TIF1γ) antibodies are associated with an increased risk of malignancy and dysphagia in patients with DM. We report an 82-year-old woman with anti-TIF1γ-positive DM who initially presented with generalized edema, followed by progressive dysphagia and proximal muscle weakness. Skin manifestations, anti-TIF1γ antibody positivity, electromyography, muscle magnetic resonance imaging, and muscle biopsy established the diagnosis of DM. Subsequent malignancy screening identified ovarian cancer. Despite immunotherapy, severe dysphagia persisted and required prolonged nasogastric tube feeding. This case highlights generalized edema as an early manifestation of anti-TIF1γ-positive DM and suggests that it may precede more typical manifestations of the disease, potentially leading to diagnostic delay.

items.title: Cytokine and genetic crosstalk in patients with coexistent familial Mediterranean fever and celiac disease: a cross-sectional study from Türkiye.
items.abstract: Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) and Celiac Disease (CD) are two distinct inflammatory disorders that arise through different immunological pathways, yet they show a notable tendency to coexist, particularly in Mediterranean populations. The immunological consequences of this coexistence have not been adequately characterized. We set out to compare serum cytokine profiles and explore potential genetic interactions in patients with both FMF and CD versus those with FMF alone or CD alone. One hundred adult patients were enrolled and divided into three groups: 40 with coexistent FMF and CD, 30 with FMF only, and 30 with CD only. Serum concentrations of IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10 were quantified by ELISA; CRP and SAA were measured using routine laboratory methods. MEFV mutations and HLA-DQ2/DQ8 genotypes were determined by PCR. Statistical evaluations included one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni correction, multivariable linear regression incorporating a formal interaction term, and principal component analysis to visualize cytokine clustering patterns. Patients with both diseases exhibited significantly higher serum levels of IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and CRP than those in either single-disease group (all p < 0.001), while IL-10 levels were notably lower (p = 0.02). Serum amyloid A levels were also significantly elevated in the coexistence group compared with both single-disease groups (p < 0.001) and correlated strongly with CRP (r = 0.69, p < 0.001). IL-6 emerged as the strongest independent predictor of CRP elevation (adjusted β = 0.47, 95% CI 0.31-0.63, p < 0.001). Principal component analysis identified a distinct pro-inflammatory cytokine cluster unique to the coexistence group. The simultaneous presence of HLA-DQ2 and the MEFV M694V variant was associated with a significant rise in IL-6 production (p < 0.001). When FMF and CD coexist, the resulting inflammatory state is substantially amplified and dysregulated, characterized by markedly elevated IL-6 and associated with a possible interaction between MEFV and HLA loci that requires confirmation in larger, independently sampled cohorts. These observations emphasize the importance of recognizing this overlap syndrome in clinical practice.

items.title: Complement and immunoglobulin profiles in ANCA-associated vasculitis with renal involvement: a serotype-stratified analysis of disease activity and renal outcomes.
items.abstract: ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) is characterized by pauci-immune small-vessel inflammation driven predominantly by neutrophil activation, in contrast to immune-complex-mediated glomerulopathies in which complement consumption tracks disease activity and renal injury severity. Serum C3 at diagnosis has repeatedly been associated with renal and patient survival in AAV, yet it remains unresolved whether complement fractions reflect the extent of renal injury in a dose-dependent manner, as they do in lupus nephritis, and how complement relates to immunoglobulin class profiles across ANCA serotypes. This retrospective single-center cohort study included 73 patients with AAV (PR3-ANCA, n = 39; MPO-ANCA, n = 34) who had complete complement and immunoglobulin data at admission and at least 6 months of follow-up at a tertiary nephrology center. Serum C3, C4, IgG, IgA, and IgM were measured at baseline before the initiation of immunosuppressive treatment; no sample was obtained after plasma exchange had begun. Patients were stratified by ANCA serotype and chronic kidney disease (CKD) severity. Associations with disease activity, inflammatory indices, and 6-month outcomes were explored using non-parametric comparisons, Spearman correlations, false discovery rate (FDR) correction, and sensitivity analyses. C3 and C4 lay within the reference interval in 97.3% and 86.3% of patients, respectively, and showed no gradient across CKD severity groups (C3 p = 0.453; C4 p = 0.550), whereas the inflammatory indices C-NLR and PLR differed across those groups. IgA was nominally higher in patients with MPO-ANCA than in those with PR3-ANCA (2.60 [1.92-2.88] vs. 2.11 [1.78-2.30] g/L, p = 0.011) but did not retain significance after FDR adjustment across the five immune parameters (q = 0.055), and all values lay within the reference interval. IgG correlated with ESR (ρ = +0.40, p < 0.001) and ΔeGFR at 6 months (ρ = +0.26, p = 0.037). Serum C4 was higher in the eight patients who did not achieve clinical remission (0.35 [0.28-0.44] vs. 0.28 [0.20-0.33] g/L, nominal p = 0.037; FDR q = 0.184; AUC 0.729, 95% bootstrap CI 0.473-0.953, an interval that includes 0.5). C3 correlated inversely with neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) (ρ = -0.24, p = 0.043). Frank complement consumption was uncommon in this cohort, and neither C3 nor C4 graded renal injury severity, consistent with pauci-immune pathogenesis and in contrast to lupus nephritis. These data do not conflict with published cohorts in which relatively lower C3 predicted adverse renal outcomes; rather, they suggest that the prognostic signal resides in variation within the reference interval rather than in measurable consumption proportional to glomerular injury. The serotype difference in IgA and the association between C4 and failure to achieve remission are exploratory observations that did not withstand correction for multiple comparisons. Because induction-regimen coding was sparse and heterogeneous, no treatment-adjusted IgA model was retained. The C4 association was based on only eight non-remission events and, notably, ran in the opposite direction to a complement-consumption interpretation; it requires confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts.
